      .Sp
      **-march=native** causes the compiler to auto-detect the architecture
      of the build computer.  At present, this feature is only supported on
      GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized.  If the auto-detect
      is unsuccessful the option has no effect.
* **-mtune=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mtune=name"
  This option specifies the name of the target \s-1ARM\s0 processor for
  which \s-1GCC\s0 should tune the performance of the code.
  For some \s-1ARM\s0 implementations better performance can be obtained by using
  this option.
  Permissible names are: **arm7tdmi**, **arm7tdmi-s**, **arm710t**,
  **arm720t**, **arm740t**, **strongarm**, **strongarm110**,
  **strongarm1100**, 0**strongarm1110**, **arm8**, **arm810**,
  **arm9**, **arm9e**, **arm920**, **arm920t**, **arm922t**,
  **arm946e-s**, **arm966e-s**, **arm968e-s**, **arm926ej-s**,
  **arm940t**, **arm9tdmi**, **arm10tdmi**, **arm1020t**,
  **arm1026ej-s**, **arm10e**, **arm1020e**, **arm1022e**,
  **arm1136j-s**, **arm1136jf-s**, **mpcore**, **mpcorenovfp**,
  **arm1156t2-s**, **arm1156t2f-s**, **arm1176jz-s**, **arm1176jzf-s**,
  **generic-armv7-a**, **cortex-a5**, **cortex-a7**, **cortex-a8**,
  **cortex-a9**, **cortex-a12**, **cortex-a15**, **cortex-a17**,
  **cortex-a32**, **cortex-a35**, **cortex-a53**, **cortex-a55**,
  **cortex-a57**, **cortex-a72**, **cortex-a73**, **cortex-a75**,
  **cortex-a76**, **ares**, **cortex-r4**, **cortex-r4f**,
  **cortex-r5**, **cortex-r7**, **cortex-r8**, **cortex-r52**,
  **cortex-m0**, **cortex-m0plus**, **cortex-m1**, **cortex-m3**,
  **cortex-m4**, **cortex-m7**, **cortex-m23**, **cortex-m33**,
  **cortex-m1.small-multiply**, **cortex-m0.small-multiply**,
  **cortex-m0plus.small-multiply**, **exynos-m1**, **marvell-pj4**,
  **neoverse-n1**, **xscale**, **iwmmxt**, **iwmmxt2**,
  **ep9312**, **fa526**, **fa626**, **fa606te**, **fa626te**,
  **fmp626**, **fa726te**, **xgene1**.
  .Sp
  Additionally, this option can specify that \s-1GCC\s0 should tune the performance
  of the code for a big.LITTLE system.  Permissible names are:
  **cortex-a15.cortex-a7**, **cortex-a17.cortex-a7**,
  **cortex-a57.cortex-a53**, **cortex-a72.cortex-a53**,
  **cortex-a72.cortex-a35**, **cortex-a73.cortex-a53**,
  **cortex-a75.cortex-a55**, **cortex-a76.cortex-a55**.
  .Sp
  **-mtune=generic-**_arch_ specifies that \s-1GCC\s0 should tune the
  performance for a blend of processors within architecture _arch_.
  The aim is to generate code that run well on the current most popular
  processors, balancing between optimizations that benefit some CPUs in the
  range, and avoiding performance pitfalls of other CPUs.  The effects of
  this option may change in future \s-1GCC\s0 versions as \s-1CPU\s0 models come and go.
  .Sp
  **-mtune** permits the same extension options as **-mcpu**, but
  the extension options do not affect the tuning of the generated code.
  .Sp
  **-mtune=native** causes the compiler to auto-detect the \s-1CPU\s0
  of the build computer.  At present, this feature is only supported on
  GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized.  If the auto-detect is
  unsuccessful the option has no effect.
* **-mcpu=**_name_[**+extension...**]  
  .IX Item "-mcpu=name[+extension...]"
  This specifies the name of the target \s-1ARM\s0 processor.  \s-1GCC\s0 uses this name
  to derive the name of the target \s-1ARM\s0 architecture (as if specified
  by **-march**) and the \s-1ARM\s0 processor type for which to tune for
  performance (as if specified by **-mtune**).  Where this option
  is used in conjunction with **-march** or **-mtune**,
  those options take precedence over the appropriate part of this option.
  .Sp
  Many of the supported CPUs implement optional architectural
  extensions.  Where this is so the architectural extensions are
  normally enabled by default.  If implementations that lack the
  extension exist, then the extension syntax can be used to disable
  those extensions that have been omitted.  For floating-point and
  Advanced \s-1SIMD\s0 (Neon) instructions, the settings of the options
  **-mfloat-abi** and **-mfpu** must also be considered:
  floating-point and Advanced \s-1SIMD\s0 instructions will only be used if
  **-mfloat-abi** is not set to **soft**; and any setting of
  **-mfpu** other than **auto** will override the available
  floating-point and \s-1SIMD\s0 extension instructions.
  .Sp
  For example, **cortex-a9** can be found in three major
  configurations: integer only, with just a floating-point unit or with
  floating-point and Advanced \s-1SIMD.\s0  The default is to enable all the
  instructions, but the extensions **+nosimd** and **+nofp** can
  be used to disable just the \s-1SIMD\s0 or both the \s-1SIMD\s0 and floating-point
  instructions respectively.
  .Sp
  Permissible names for this option are the same as those for
  **-mtune**.
  .Sp
  The following extension options are common to the listed CPUs:
    * **+nodsp**  
      .IX Item "+nodsp"
      Disable the \s-1DSP\s0 instructions on **cortex-m33**.
    * **+nofp**  
      .IX Item "+nofp"
      Disables the floating-point instructions on **arm9e**,
      **arm946e-s**, **arm966e-s**, **arm968e-s**, **arm10e**,
      **arm1020e**, **arm1022e**, **arm926ej-s**,
      **arm1026ej-s**, **cortex-r5**, **cortex-r7**, **cortex-r8**,
      **cortex-m4**, **cortex-m7** and **cortex-m33**.
      Disables the floating-point and \s-1SIMD\s0 instructions on
      **generic-armv7-a**, **cortex-a5**, **cortex-a7**,
      **cortex-a8**, **cortex-a9**, **cortex-a12**,
      **cortex-a15**, **cortex-a17**, **cortex-a15.cortex-a7**,
      **cortex-a17.cortex-a7**, **cortex-a32**, **cortex-a35**,
      **cortex-a53** and **cortex-a55**.
    * **+nofp.dp**  
      .IX Item "+nofp.dp"
      Disables the double-precision component of the floating-point instructions
      on **cortex-r5**, **cortex-r7**, **cortex-r8**, **cortex-r52** and
      **cortex-m7**.
    * **+nosimd**  
      .IX Item "+nosimd"
      Disables the \s-1SIMD\s0 (but not floating-point) instructions on
      **generic-armv7-a**, **cortex-a5**, **cortex-a7**
      and **cortex-a9**.
    * **+crypto**  
      .IX Item "+crypto"
      Enables the cryptographic instructions on **cortex-a32**,
      **cortex-a35**, **cortex-a53**, **cortex-a55**, **cortex-a57**,
      **cortex-a72**, **cortex-a73**, **cortex-a75**, **exynos-m1**,
      **xgene1**, **cortex-a57.cortex-a53**, **cortex-a72.cortex-a53**,
      **cortex-a73.cortex-a35**, **cortex-a73.cortex-a53** and
      **cortex-a75.cortex-a55**.
      .Sp
      Additionally the **generic-armv7-a** pseudo target defaults to
      VFPv3 with 16 double-precision registers.  It supports the following
      extension options: **mp**, **sec**, **vfpv3-d16**,
      **vfpv3**, **vfpv3-d16-fp16**, **vfpv3-fp16**,
      **vfpv4-d16**, **vfpv4**, **neon**, **neon-vfpv3**,
      **neon-fp16**, **neon-vfpv4**.  The meanings are the same as for
      the extensions to **-march=armv7-a**.
      .Sp
      **-mcpu=generic-**_arch_ is also permissible, and is
      equivalent to **-march=**_arch_ **-mtune=generic-**_arch_.
      See **-mtune** for more information.
      .Sp
      **-mcpu=native** causes the compiler to auto-detect the \s-1CPU\s0
      of the build computer.  At present, this feature is only supported on
      GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized.  If the auto-detect
      is unsuccessful the option has no effect.
* **-mfpu=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mfpu=name"
  This specifies what floating-point hardware (or hardware emulation) is
  available on the target.  Permissible names are: **auto**, **vfpv2**,
  **vfpv3**,
  **vfpv3-fp16**, **vfpv3-d16**, **vfpv3-d16-fp16**, **vfpv3xd**,
  **vfpv3xd-fp16**, **neon-vfpv3**, **neon-fp16**, **vfpv4**,
  **vfpv4-d16**, **fpv4-sp-d16**, **neon-vfpv4**,
  **fpv5-d16**, **fpv5-sp-d16**,
  **fp-armv8**, **neon-fp-armv8** and **crypto-neon-fp-armv8**.
  Note that **neon** is an alias for **neon-vfpv3** and **vfp**
  is an alias for **vfpv2**.
  .Sp
  The setting **auto** is the default and is special.  It causes the
  compiler to select the floating-point and Advanced \s-1SIMD\s0 instructions
  based on the settings of **-mcpu** and **-march**.
  .Sp
  If the selected floating-point hardware includes the \s-1NEON\s0 extension
  (e.g. **-mfpu=neon**), note that floating-point
  operations are not generated by \s-1GCC\s0's auto-vectorization pass unless
  **-funsafe-math-optimizations** is also specified.  This is
  because \s-1NEON\s0 hardware does not fully implement the \s-1IEEE 754\s0 standard for
  floating-point arithmetic (in particular denormal values are treated as
  zero), so the use of \s-1NEON\s0 instructions may lead to a loss of precision.
  .Sp
  You can also set the fpu name at function level by using the \f(CW`target("fpu=")\*(C' function attributes or pragmas.
* **-mfp16-format=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mfp16-format=name"
  Specify the format of the \f(CW`\_\|\_fp16\*(C' half-precision floating-point type.
  Permissible names are **none**, **ieee**, and **alternative**;
  the default is **none**, in which case the \f(CW`\_\|\_fp16\*(C' type is not
  defined.
* **-mstructure-size-boundary=**_n_  
  .IX Item "-mstructure-size-boundary=n"
  The sizes of all structures and unions are rounded up to a multiple
  of the number of bits set by this option.  Permissible values are 8, 32
  and 64.  The default value varies for different toolchains.  For the \s-1COFF\s0
  targeted toolchain the default value is 8.  A value of 64 is only allowed
  if the underlying \s-1ABI\s0 supports it.
  .Sp
  Specifying a larger number can produce faster, more efficient code, but
  can also increase the size of the program.  Different values are potentially
  incompatible.  Code compiled with one value cannot necessarily expect to
  work with code or libraries compiled with another value, if they exchange
  information using structures or unions.
  .Sp
  This option is deprecated.
* **-mabort-on-noreturn**  
  .IX Item "-mabort-on-noreturn"
  Generate a call to the function \f(CW`abort\*(C' at the end of a
  \f(CW`noreturn\*(C' function.  It is executed if the function tries to
  return.
* **-mlong-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mlong-calls"
* **-mno-long-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mno-long-calls"
  Tells the compiler to perform function calls by first loading the
  address of the function into a register and then performing a subroutine
  call on this register.  This switch is needed if the target function
  lies outside of the 64-megabyte addressing range of the offset-based
  version of subroutine call instruction.
  .Sp
  Even if this switch is enabled, not all function calls are turned
  into long calls.  The heuristic is that static functions, functions
  that have the \f(CW`short\_call\*(C' attribute, functions that are inside
  the scope of a \f(CW`#pragma no\_long\_calls\*(C' directive, and functions whose
  definitions have already been compiled within the current compilation
  unit are not turned into long calls.  The exceptions to this rule are
  that weak function definitions, functions with the \f(CW`long\_call\*(C'
  attribute or the \f(CW`section\*(C' attribute, and functions that are within
  the scope of a \f(CW`#pragma long\_calls\*(C' directive are always
  turned into long calls.
  .Sp
  This feature is not enabled by default.  Specifying
  **-mno-long-calls** restores the default behavior, as does
  placing the function calls within the scope of a \f(CW`#pragma
  long\_calls\_off directive.  Note these switches have no effect on how
  the compiler generates code to handle function calls via function
  pointers.
* **-msingle-pic-base**  
  .IX Item "-msingle-pic-base"
  Treat the register used for \s-1PIC\s0 addressing as read-only, rather than
  loading it in the prologue for each function.  The runtime system is
  responsible for initializing this register with an appropriate value
  before execution begins.
* **-mpic-register=**_reg_  
  .IX Item "-mpic-register=reg"
  Specify the register to be used for \s-1PIC\s0 addressing.
  For standard \s-1PIC\s0 base case, the default is any suitable register
  determined by compiler.  For single \s-1PIC\s0 base case, the default is
  **R9** if target is \s-1EABI\s0 based or stack-checking is enabled,
  otherwise the default is **R10**.
* **-mpic-data-is-text-relative**  
  .IX Item "-mpic-data-is-text-relative"
  Assume that the displacement between the text and data segments is fixed
  at static link time.  This permits using PC-relative addressing
  operations to access data known to be in the data segment.  For
  non-VxWorks \s-1RTP\s0 targets, this option is enabled by default.  When
  disabled on such targets, it will enable **-msingle-pic-base** by
  default.
* **-mpoke-function-name**  
  .IX Item "-mpoke-function-name"
  Write the name of each function into the text section, directly
  preceding the function prologue.  The generated code is similar to this:
  .Sp
  .Vb 9
               t0
                   .ascii "arm_poke_function_name", 0
                   .align
               t1
                   .word 0xff000000 + (t1 - t0)
               arm_poke_function_name
                   mov     ip, sp
                   stmfd   sp!, {fp, ip, lr, pc}
                   sub     fp, ip, #4
  .Ve
  .Sp
  When performing a stack backtrace, code can inspect the value of
  \f(CW`pc\*(C' stored at \f(CW\*(C\`fp + 0\*(C'.  If the trace function then looks at
  location \f(CW`pc - 12\*(C' and the top 8 bits are set, then we know that
  there is a function name embedded immediately preceding this location
  and has length \f(CW`((pc[-3]) & 0xff000000)\*(C'.
* **-mthumb**  
  .IX Item "-mthumb"
* **-marm**  
  .IX Item "-marm"
  Select between generating code that executes in \s-1ARM\s0 and Thumb
  states.  The default for most configurations is to generate code
  that executes in \s-1ARM\s0 state, but the default can be changed by
  configuring \s-1GCC\s0 with the **--with-mode=**_state_
  configure option.
  .Sp
  You can also override the \s-1ARM\s0 and Thumb mode for each function
  by using the \f(CW`target("thumb")\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`target("arm")\*(C' function attributes or pragmas.
* **-mflip-thumb**  
  .IX Item "-mflip-thumb"
  Switch ARM/Thumb modes on alternating functions.
  This option is provided for regression testing of mixed Thumb/ARM code
  generation, and is not intended for ordinary use in compiling code.
* **-mtpcs-frame**  
  .IX Item "-mtpcs-frame"
  Generate a stack frame that is compliant with the Thumb Procedure Call
  Standard for all non-leaf functions.  (A leaf function is one that does
  not call any other functions.)  The default is **-mno-tpcs-frame**.
* **-mtpcs-leaf-frame**  
  .IX Item "-mtpcs-leaf-frame"
  Generate a stack frame that is compliant with the Thumb Procedure Call
  Standard for all leaf functions.  (A leaf function is one that does
  not call any other functions.)  The default is **-mno-apcs-leaf-frame**.
* **-mcallee-super-interworking**  
  .IX Item "-mcallee-super-interworking"
  Gives all externally visible functions in the file being compiled an \s-1ARM\s0
  instruction set header which switches to Thumb mode before executing the
  rest of the function.  This allows these functions to be called from
  non-interworking code.  This option is not valid in \s-1AAPCS\s0 configurations
  because interworking is enabled by default.
* **-mcaller-super-interworking**  
  .IX Item "-mcaller-super-interworking"
  Allows calls via function pointers (including virtual functions) to
  execute correctly regardless of whether the target code has been
  compiled for interworking or not.  There is a small overhead in the cost
  of executing a function pointer if this option is enabled.  This option
  is not valid in \s-1AAPCS\s0 configurations because interworking is enabled
  by default.
* **-mtp=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mtp=name"
  Specify the access model for the thread local storage pointer.  The valid
  models are **soft**, which generates calls to \f(CW`\_\|\_aeabi\_read\_tp\*(C',
  **cp15**, which fetches the thread pointer from \f(CW`cp15\*(C' directly
  (supported in the arm6k architecture), and **auto**, which uses the
  best available method for the selected processor.  The default setting is
  **auto**.
* **-mtls-dialect=**_dialect_  
  .IX Item "-mtls-dialect=dialect"
  Specify the dialect to use for accessing thread local storage.  Two
  _dialect_s are supported---**gnu** and **gnu2**.  The
  **gnu** dialect selects the original \s-1GNU\s0 scheme for supporting
  local and global dynamic \s-1TLS\s0 models.  The **gnu2** dialect
  selects the \s-1GNU\s0 descriptor scheme, which provides better performance
  for shared libraries.  The \s-1GNU\s0 descriptor scheme is compatible with
  the original scheme, but does require new assembler, linker and
  library support.  Initial and local exec \s-1TLS\s0 models are unaffected by
  this option and always use the original scheme.
* **-mword-relocations**  
  .IX Item "-mword-relocations"
  Only generate absolute relocations on word-sized values (i.e. R_ARM_ABS32).
  This is enabled by default on targets (uClinux, SymbianOS) where the runtime
  loader imposes this restriction, and when **-fpic** or **-fPIC**
  is specified. This option conflicts with **-mslow-flash-data**.
* **-mfix-cortex-m3-ldrd**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-cortex-m3-ldrd"
  Some Cortex-M3 cores can cause data corruption when \f(CW`ldrd\*(C' instructions
  with overlapping destination and base registers are used.  This option avoids
  generating these instructions.  This option is enabled by default when
  **-mcpu=cortex-m3** is specified.
* **-munaligned-access**  
  .IX Item "-munaligned-access"
* **-mno-unaligned-access**  
  .IX Item "-mno-unaligned-access"
  Enables (or disables) reading and writing of 16- and 32- bit values
  from addresses that are not 16- or 32- bit aligned.  By default
  unaligned access is disabled for all pre-ARMv6, all ARMv6-M and for
  ARMv8-M Baseline architectures, and enabled for all other
  architectures.  If unaligned access is not enabled then words in packed
  data structures are accessed a byte at a time.
  .Sp
  The \s-1ARM\s0 attribute \f(CW`Tag\_CPU\_unaligned\_access\*(C' is set in the
  generated object file to either true or false, depending upon the
  setting of this option.  If unaligned access is enabled then the
  preprocessor symbol \f(CW`\_\|\_ARM\_FEATURE\_UNALIGNED\*(C' is also
  defined.
* **-mneon-for-64bits**  
  .IX Item "-mneon-for-64bits"
  Enables using Neon to handle scalar 64-bits operations. This is
  disabled by default since the cost of moving data from core registers
  to Neon is high.
* **-mslow-flash-data**  
  .IX Item "-mslow-flash-data"
  Assume loading data from flash is slower than fetching instruction.
  Therefore literal load is minimized for better performance.
  This option is only supported when compiling for ARMv7 M-profile and
  off by default. It conflicts with **-mword-relocations**.
* **-masm-syntax-unified**  
  .IX Item "-masm-syntax-unified"
  Assume inline assembler is using unified asm syntax.  The default is
  currently off which implies divided syntax.  This option has no impact
  on Thumb2. However, this may change in future releases of \s-1GCC.\s0
  Divided syntax should be considered deprecated.
* **-mrestrict-it**  
  .IX Item "-mrestrict-it"
  Restricts generation of \s-1IT\s0 blocks to conform to the rules of ARMv8-A.
  \s-1IT\s0 blocks can only contain a single 16-bit instruction from a select
  set of instructions. This option is on by default for ARMv8-A Thumb mode.
* **-mprint-tune-info**  
  .IX Item "-mprint-tune-info"
  Print \s-1CPU\s0 tuning information as comment in assembler file.  This is
  an option used only for regression testing of the compiler and not
  intended for ordinary use in compiling code.  This option is disabled
  by default.
* **-mverbose-cost-dump**  
  .IX Item "-mverbose-cost-dump"
  Enable verbose cost model dumping in the debug dump files.  This option is
  provided for use in debugging the compiler.
* **-mpure-code**  
  .IX Item "-mpure-code"
  Do not allow constant data to be placed in code sections.
  Additionally, when compiling for \s-1ELF\s0 object format give all text sections the
  \s-1ELF\s0 processor-specific section attribute \f(CW`SHF\_ARM\_PURECODE\*(C'.  This option
  is only available when generating non-pic code for M-profile targets with the
  \s-1MOVT\s0 instruction.
* **-mcmse**  
  .IX Item "-mcmse"
  Generate secure code as per the ARMv8-M Security Extensions: Requirements on
  Development Tools Engineering Specification, which can be found on
  &lt;**http://infocenter.arm.com/help/topic/com.arm.doc.ecm0359818/ECM0359818\_armv8m\_security\_extensions\_reqs\_on\_dev\_tools\_1\_0.pdf**&gt;.

<a name="s-1avrs0-options"></a>

### \s-1AVR\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "AVR Options"
These options are defined for \s-1AVR\s0 implementations:

* **-mmcu=**_mcu_  
  .IX Item "-mmcu=mcu"
  Specify Atmel \s-1AVR\s0 instruction set architectures (\s-1ISA\s0) or \s-1MCU\s0 type.
  .Sp
  The default for this option is@tie{}**avr2**.
  .Sp
  \s-1GCC\s0 supports the following \s-1AVR\s0 devices and ISAs:
      .ie n .IP """avr2""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr2" 4
      .IX Item "avr2"
      Classic\*(R" devices with up to 8@tie{}KiB of program memory.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`attiny22\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny26\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90c8534\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s2313\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s2323\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s2333\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s2343\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s4414\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s4433\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s4434\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s8515\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s8535\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr25""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr25" 4
      .IX Item "avr25"
      Classic\*(R" devices with up to 8@tie{}KiB of program memory and with the \f(CW\*(C\`MOVW\*(C' instruction.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`ata5272\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6616c\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny13\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny13a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny2313\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny2313a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny24\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny24a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny25\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny261\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny261a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny43u\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny4313\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny44\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny44a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny441\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny45\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny461\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny461a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny48\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny828\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny84\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny84a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny841\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny85\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny861\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny861a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny87\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny88\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at86rf401\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr3""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr3" 4
      .IX Item "avr3"
      Classic\*(R" devices with 16@tie{}KiB up to 64@tie{}KiB of  program memory.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`at43usb355\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at76c711\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr31""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr31" 4
      .IX Item "avr31"
      Classic\*(R" devices with 128@tie{}KiB of program memory.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`atmega103\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at43usb320\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr35""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr35" 4
      .IX Item "avr35"
      Classic\*(R" devices with 16@tie{}KiB up to 64@tie{}KiB of program memory and with the \f(CW\*(C\`MOVW\*(C' instruction.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`ata5505\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6617c\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata664251\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16u2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega32u2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8u2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny1634\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny167\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90usb162\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90usb82\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr4""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr4" 4
      .IX Item "avr4"
      Enhanced\*(R" devices with up to 8@tie{}KiB of program memory.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`ata6285\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6286\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6289\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6612c\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega48\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega48a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega48p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega48pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega48pb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8hva\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8515\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega8535\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega88\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega88a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega88p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega88pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega88pb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm1\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm2b\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm3\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm3b\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90pwm81\*(C'.
      .ie n .IP """avr5""" 4
      .el .IP "\f(CWavr5" 4
      .IX Item "avr5"
      Enhanced\*(R" devices with 16@tie{}KiB up to 64@tie{}KiB of program memory.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`ata5702m322\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5782\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5790\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5790n\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5791\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5795\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata5831\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6613c\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata6614q\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata8210\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ata8510\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16hva\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16hva2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16hvb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16hvbrevb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16m1\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega16u4\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega161\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega162\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega163\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega164a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega164p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega164pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega165\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega165a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega165p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega165pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega168\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega168a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega168p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega168pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega168pb\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega169\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega169a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega169p\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega169pa\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega32\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega32a\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`atmega32c1\*(C',       _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`attiny10\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny20\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny4\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny40\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny5\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny9\*(C'.

      This \s-1ISA\s0 is implemented by the minimal \s-1AVR\s0 core and supported for assembler only.
      _mcu_\f(CW@tie{}= \f(CW`attiny11\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny12\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny15\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`attiny28\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`at90s1200\*(C'.
* **-mabsdata**  
  .IX Item "-mabsdata"
  Assume that all data in static storage can be accessed by \s-1LDS / STS\s0
  instructions.  This option has only an effect on reduced Tiny devices like
  ATtiny40.  See also the \f(CW`absdata\*(C'
  **\s-1AVR\s0 Variable Attributes,variable attribute**.
* **-maccumulate-args**  
  .IX Item "-maccumulate-args"
  Accumulate outgoing function arguments and acquire/release the needed
  stack space for outgoing function arguments once in function
  prologue/epilogue.  Without this option, outgoing arguments are pushed
  before calling a function and popped afterwards.
  .Sp
  Popping the arguments after the function call can be expensive on
  \s-1AVR\s0 so that accumulating the stack space might lead to smaller
  executables because arguments need not be removed from the
  stack after such a function call.
  .Sp
  This option can lead to reduced code size for functions that perform
  several calls to functions that get their arguments on the stack like
  calls to printf-like functions.
* **-mbranch-cost=**_cost_  
  .IX Item "-mbranch-cost=cost"
  Set the branch costs for conditional branch instructions to
  _cost_.  Reasonable values for _cost_ are small, non-negative
  integers. The default branch cost is 0.
* **-mcall-prologues**  
  .IX Item "-mcall-prologues"
  Functions prologues/epilogues are expanded as calls to appropriate
  subroutines.  Code size is smaller.
* **-mgas-isr-prologues**  
  .IX Item "-mgas-isr-prologues"
  Interrupt service routines (ISRs) may use the \f(CW`\_\|\_gcc\_isr\*(C' pseudo
  instruction supported by \s-1GNU\s0 Binutils.
  If this option is on, the feature can still be disabled for individual
  ISRs by means of the **\s-1AVR\s0 Function Attributes,,\f(CB`no\_gccisr\*(C'**
  function attribute.  This feature is activated per default
  if optimization is on (but not with **-Og**, \f(CW@pxref{Optimize Options}),
  and if \s-1GNU\s0 Binutils support \s-1PR21683\s0 (\f(CW`https://sourceware.org/PR21683\*(C').
* **-mint8**  
  .IX Item "-mint8"
  Assume \f(CW`int\*(C' to be 8-bit integer.  This affects the sizes of all types: a
  \f(CW`char\*(C' is 1 byte, an \f(CW\*(C\`int\*(C' is 1 byte, a \f(CW\*(C\`long\*(C' is 2 bytes,
  and \f(CW`long long\*(C' is 4 bytes.  Please note that this option does not
  conform to the C standards, but it results in smaller code
  size.
* **-mmain-is-OS\_task**  
  .IX Item "-mmain-is-OS_task"
  Do not save registers in \f(CW`main\*(C'.  The effect is the same like
  attaching attribute **\s-1AVR\s0 Function Attributes,,\f(CB`OS\_task\*(C'**
  to \f(CW`main\*(C'. It is activated per default if optimization is on.
* **-mn-flash=**_num_  
  .IX Item "-mn-flash=num"
  Assume that the flash memory has a size of 
  _num_ times 64@tie{}KiB.
* **-mno-interrupts**  
  .IX Item "-mno-interrupts"
  Generated code is not compatible with hardware interrupts.
  Code size is smaller.
* **-mrelax**  
  .IX Item "-mrelax"
  Try to replace \f(CW`CALL\*(C' resp. \f(CW\*(C\`JMP\*(C' instruction by the shorter
  \f(CW`RCALL\*(C' resp. \f(CW\*(C\`RJMP\*(C' instruction if applicable.
  Setting **-mrelax** just adds the **--mlink-relax** option to
  the assembler's command line and the **--relax** option to the
  linker's command line.
  .Sp
  Jump relaxing is performed by the linker because jump offsets are not
  known before code is located. Therefore, the assembler code generated by the
  compiler is the same, but the instructions in the executable may
  differ from instructions in the assembler code.
  .Sp
  Relaxing must be turned on if linker stubs are needed, see the
  section on \f(CW`EIND\*(C' and linker stubs below.
* **-mrmw**  
  .IX Item "-mrmw"
  Assume that the device supports the Read-Modify-Write
  instructions \f(CW`XCH\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`LAC\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`LAS\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`LAT\*(C'.
* **-mshort-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mshort-calls"
  Assume that \f(CW`RJMP\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`RCALL\*(C' can target the whole
  program memory.
  .Sp
  This option is used internally for multilib selection.  It is
  not an optimization option, and you don't need to set it by hand.
* **-msp8**  
  .IX Item "-msp8"
  Treat the stack pointer register as an 8-bit register,
  i.e. assume the high byte of the stack pointer is zero.
  In general, you don't need to set this option by hand.
  .Sp
  This option is used internally by the compiler to select and
  build multilibs for architectures \f(CW`avr2\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`avr25\*(C'.
  These architectures mix devices with and without \f(CW`SPH\*(C'.
  For any setting other than **-mmcu=avr2** or **-mmcu=avr25**
  the compiler driver adds or removes this option from the compiler
  proper's command line, because the compiler then knows if the device
  or architecture has an 8-bit stack pointer and thus no \f(CW`SPH\*(C'
  register or not.
* **-mstrict-X**  
  .IX Item "-mstrict-X"
  Use address register \f(CW`X\*(C' in a way proposed by the hardware.  This means
  that \f(CW`X\*(C' is only used in indirect, post-increment or
  pre-decrement addressing.
  .Sp
  Without this option, the \f(CW`X\*(C' register may be used in the same way
  as \f(CW`Y\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`Z\*(C' which then is emulated by additional
  instructions.  
  For example, loading a value with \f(CW`X+const\*(C' addressing with a
  small non-negative \f(CW`const &lt; 64\*(C' to a register _Rn_ is
  performed as
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          adiw r26, const   ; X += const
          ld   &lt;Rn&gt;, X        ; &lt;Rn&gt; = *X
          sbiw r26, const   ; X -= const
  .Ve
* **-mtiny-stack**  
  .IX Item "-mtiny-stack"
  Only change the lower 8@tie{}bits of the stack pointer.
* **-mfract-convert-truncate**  
  .IX Item "-mfract-convert-truncate"
  Allow to use truncation instead of rounding towards zero for fractional fixed-point types.
* **-nodevicelib**  
  .IX Item "-nodevicelib"
  Don't link against AVR-LibC's device specific library \f(CW`lib&lt;mcu&gt;.a\*(C'.
* **-Waddr-space-convert**  
  .IX Item "-Waddr-space-convert"
  Warn about conversions between address spaces in the case where the
  resulting address space is not contained in the incoming address space.
* **-Wmisspelled-isr**  
  .IX Item "-Wmisspelled-isr"
  Warn if the \s-1ISR\s0 is misspelled, i.e. without _\|_vector prefix.
  Enabled by default.

\f(CW`EIND\*(C' and Devices with More Than 128 Ki Bytes of Flash
.IX Subsection "EIND and Devices with More Than 128 Ki Bytes of Flash"

Pointers in the implementation are 16@tie{}bits wide.
The address of a function or label is represented as word address so
that indirect jumps and calls can target any code address in the
range of 64@tie{}Ki words.

In order to facilitate indirect jump on devices with more than 128@tie{}Ki
bytes of program memory space, there is a special function register called
\f(CW`EIND\*(C' that serves as most significant part of the target address
when \f(CW`EICALL\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`EIJMP\*(C' instructions are used.

Indirect jumps and calls on these devices are handled as follows by
the compiler and are subject to some limitations:

* *  
  The compiler never sets \f(CW`EIND\*(C'.
* *  
  The compiler uses \f(CW`EIND\*(C' implicitly in \f(CW\*(C\`EICALL\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`EIJMP\*(C'
  instructions or might read \f(CW`EIND\*(C' directly in order to emulate an
  indirect call/jump by means of a \f(CW`RET\*(C' instruction.
* *  
  The compiler assumes that \f(CW`EIND\*(C' never changes during the startup
  code or during the application. In particular, \f(CW`EIND\*(C' is not
  saved/restored in function or interrupt service routine
  prologue/epilogue.
* *  
  For indirect calls to functions and computed goto, the linker
  generates _stubs_. Stubs are jump pads sometimes also called
  _trampolines_. Thus, the indirect call/jump jumps to such a stub.
  The stub contains a direct jump to the desired address.
* *  
  Linker relaxation must be turned on so that the linker generates
  the stubs correctly in all situations. See the compiler option
  **-mrelax** and the linker option **--relax**.
  There are corner cases where the linker is supposed to generate stubs
  but aborts without relaxation and without a helpful error message.
* *  
  The default linker script is arranged for code with \f(CW`EIND = 0\*(C'.
  If code is supposed to work for a setup with \f(CW`EIND != 0\*(C', a custom
  linker script has to be used in order to place the sections whose
  name start with \f(CW`.trampolines\*(C' into the segment where \f(CW\*(C\`EIND\*(C'
  points to.
* *  
  The startup code from libgcc never sets \f(CW`EIND\*(C'.
  Notice that startup code is a blend of code from libgcc and AVR-LibC.
  For the impact of AVR-LibC on \f(CW`EIND\*(C', see the
  AVR-LibC&nbsp;user&nbsp;manual (\f(CW`http://nongnu.org/avr-libc/user-manual/\*(C').
* *  
  It is legitimate for user-specific startup code to set up \f(CW`EIND\*(C'
  early, for example by means of initialization code located in
  section \f(CW`.init3\*(C'. Such code runs prior to general startup code
  that initializes \s-1RAM\s0 and calls constructors, but after the bit
  of startup code from AVR-LibC that sets \f(CW`EIND\*(C' to the segment
  where the vector table is located.
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          #include &lt;avr/io.h&gt;
          
          static void
          _\|_attribute_\|_((section(".init3"),naked,used,no_instrument_function))
          init3_set_eind (void)
          {
            _\|_asm volatile ("ldi r24,pm_hh8(_\|_trampolines_start)\en\et"
                            "out %i0,r24" :: "n" (&EIND) : "r24","memory");
          }
  .Ve
  .Sp
  The \f(CW`\_\|\_trampolines\_start\*(C' symbol is defined in the linker script.
* *  
  Stubs are generated automatically by the linker if
  the following two conditions are met:
      .ie n .IP "-&lt;The address of a label is taken by means of the ""gs"" modifier&gt;" 4
      .el .IP "-&lt;The address of a label is taken by means of the \f(CWgs modifier&gt;" 4
      .IX Item "-&lt;The address of a label is taken by means of the gs modifier&gt;"
      (short for _generate stubs_) like so:
      .Sp
      .Vb 2
              LDI r24, lo8(gs(&lt;func&gt;))
              LDI r25, hi8(gs(&lt;func&gt;))
      .Ve
    * -&lt;The final location of that label is in a code segment&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;The final location of that label is in a code segment&gt;"
      _outside_ the segment where the stubs are located.
* *  
  The compiler emits such \f(CW`gs\*(C' modifiers for code labels in the
  following situations:
    * -&lt;Taking address of a function or code label.&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;Taking address of a function or code label.&gt;"
    * -&lt;Computed goto.&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;Computed goto.&gt;"
    * -&lt;If prologue-save function is used, see **-mcall-prologues**&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;If prologue-save function is used, see -mcall-prologues&gt;"
      command-line option.
    * -&lt;Switch/case dispatch tables. If you do not want such dispatch&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;Switch/case dispatch tables. If you do not want such dispatch&gt;"
      tables you can specify the **-fno-jump-tables** command-line option.
    * -&lt;C and  constructors/destructors called during startup/shutdown.&gt;  
      .IX Item "-&lt;C and constructors/destructors called during startup/shutdown.&gt;"
      .ie n .IP "-&lt;If the tools hit a ""gs()"" modifier explained above.&gt;" 4
      .el .IP "-&lt;If the tools hit a \f(CWgs() modifier explained above.&gt;" 4
      .IX Item "-&lt;If the tools hit a gs() modifier explained above.&gt;"
* *  
  Jumping to non-symbolic addresses like so is _not_ supported:
  .Sp
  .Vb 5
          int main (void)
          {
              /* Call function at word address 0x2 */
              return ((int(*)(void)) 0x2)();
          }
  .Ve
  .Sp
  Instead, a stub has to be set up, i.e. the function has to be called
  through a symbol (\f(CW`func\_4\*(C' in the example):
  .Sp
  .Vb 3
          int main (void)
          {
              extern int func_4 (void);
          
              /* Call function at byte address 0x4 */
              return func_4();
          }
  .Ve
  .Sp
  and the application be linked with **-Wl,--defsym,func\_4=0x4**.
  Alternatively, \f(CW`func\_4\*(C' can be defined in the linker script.

Handling of the \f(CW`RAMPD\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPX\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPY\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPZ\*(C' Special Function Registers
.IX Subsection "Handling of the RAMPD, RAMPX, RAMPY and RAMPZ Special Function Registers"

Some \s-1AVR\s0 devices support memories larger than the 64@tie{}KiB range
that can be accessed with 16-bit pointers.  To access memory locations
outside this 64@tie{}KiB range, the content of a \f(CW`RAMP\*(C'
register is used as high part of the address:
The \f(CW`X\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`Y\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`Z\*(C' address register is concatenated
with the \f(CW`RAMPX\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPY\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPZ\*(C' special function
register, respectively, to get a wide address. Similarly,
\f(CW`RAMPD\*(C' is used together with direct addressing.

* *  
  The startup code initializes the \f(CW`RAMP\*(C' special function
  registers with zero.
* *  
  If a **\s-1AVR\s0 Named Address Spaces,named address space** other than
  generic or \f(CW`\_\|\_flash\*(C' is used, then \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPZ\*(C' is set
  as needed before the operation.
* *  
  If the device supports \s-1RAM\s0 larger than 64@tie{}KiB and the compiler
  needs to change \f(CW`RAMPZ\*(C' to accomplish an operation, \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPZ\*(C'
  is reset to zero after the operation.
* *  
  If the device comes with a specific \f(CW`RAMP\*(C' register, the \s-1ISR\s0
  prologue/epilogue saves/restores that \s-1SFR\s0 and initializes it with
  zero in case the \s-1ISR\s0 code might (implicitly) use it.
* *  
  \s-1RAM\s0 larger than 64@tie{}KiB is not supported by \s-1GCC\s0 for \s-1AVR\s0 targets.
  If you use inline assembler to read from locations outside the
  16-bit address range and change one of the \f(CW`RAMP\*(C' registers,
  you must reset it to zero after the access.

\s-1AVR\s0 Built-in Macros
.IX Subsection "AVR Built-in Macros"

\s-1GCC\s0 defines several built-in macros so that the user code can test
for the presence or absence of features.  Almost any of the following
built-in macros are deduced from device capabilities and thus
triggered by the **-mmcu=** command-line option.

For even more AVR-specific built-in macros see
**\s-1AVR\s0 Named Address Spaces** and **\s-1AVR\s0 Built-in Functions**.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_ARCH_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_ARCH\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_ARCH__"
Build-in macro that resolves to a decimal number that identifies the
architecture and depends on the **-mmcu=**_mcu_ option.
Possible values are:
.Sp
\f(CW2, \f(CW25, \f(CW3, \f(CW31, \f(CW35,
\f(CW4, \f(CW5, \f(CW51, \f(CW6
.Sp
for _mcu_=\f(CW`avr2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr25\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr3\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr31\*(C',
\f(CW`avr35\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr4\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr5\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr51\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avr6\*(C',
.Sp
respectively and
.Sp
\f(CW100,
\f(CW102, \f(CW103, \f(CW104,
\f(CW105, \f(CW106, \f(CW107
.Sp
for _mcu_=\f(CW`avrtiny\*(C',
\f(CW`avrxmega2\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avrxmega3\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avrxmega4\*(C',
\f(CW`avrxmega5\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avrxmega6\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`avrxmega7\*(C', respectively.
If _mcu_ specifies a device, this built-in macro is set
accordingly. For example, with **-mmcu=atmega8** the macro is
defined to \f(CW4.
.ie n .IP """\_\|\_AVR\__Device__\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_\f(CIDevice\f(CW\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_Device__"
Setting **-mmcu=**_device_ defines this built-in macro which reflects
the device's name. For example, **-mmcu=atmega8** defines the
built-in macro \f(CW`\_\|\_AVR\_ATmega8\_\|\_\*(C', **-mmcu=attiny261a** defines
\f(CW`\_\|\_AVR\_ATtiny261A\_\|\_\*(C', etc.
.Sp
The built-in macros' names follow
the scheme \f(CW`\_\|\_AVR\_\f(CIDevice\f(CW\_\|\_\*(C' where _Device_ is
the device name as from the \s-1AVR\s0 user manual. The difference between
_Device_ in the built-in macro and _device_ in
**-mmcu=**_device_ is that the latter is always lowercase.
.Sp
If _device_ is not a device but only a core architecture like
**avr51**, this macro is not defined.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_DEVICE_NAME_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_DEVICE\_NAME\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_DEVICE_NAME__"
Setting **-mmcu=**_device_ defines this built-in macro to
the device's name. For example, with **-mmcu=atmega8** the macro
is defined to \f(CW`atmega8\*(C'.
.Sp
If _device_ is not a device but only a core architecture like
**avr51**, this macro is not defined.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_XMEGA_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_XMEGA\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_XMEGA__"
The device / architecture belongs to the \s-1XMEGA\s0 family of devices.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_ELPM_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_ELPM\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_ELPM__"
The device has the \f(CW`ELPM\*(C' instruction.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_ELPMX_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_ELPMX\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_ELPMX__"
The device has the \f(CW`ELPM R\f(CIn\f(CW,Z\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`ELPM
R\f(CIn\f(CW,Z+ instructions.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_MOVW_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_MOVW\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_MOVW__"
The device has the \f(CW`MOVW\*(C' instruction to perform 16-bit
register-register moves.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_LPMX_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_LPMX\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_LPMX__"
The device has the \f(CW`LPM R\f(CIn\f(CW,Z\*(C' and
\f(CW`LPM R\f(CIn\f(CW,Z+\*(C' instructions.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_MUL_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_MUL\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_MUL__"
The device has a hardware multiplier.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_JMP_CALL_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_JMP\_CALL\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_JMP_CALL__"
The device has the \f(CW`JMP\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`CALL\*(C' instructions.
This is the case for devices with more than 8@tie{}KiB of program
memory.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_EIJMP_EICALL_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_EIJMP\_EICALL\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_EIJMP_EICALL__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_3_BYTE_PC_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_3\_BYTE\_PC\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_3_BYTE_PC__"
The device has the \f(CW`EIJMP\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`EICALL\*(C' instructions.
This is the case for devices with more than 128@tie{}KiB of program memory.
This also means that the program counter
(\s-1PC\s0) is 3@tie{}bytes wide.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_2_BYTE_PC_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_2\_BYTE\_PC\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_2_BYTE_PC__"
The program counter (\s-1PC\s0) is 2@tie{}bytes wide. This is the case for devices
with up to 128@tie{}KiB of program memory.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_8BIT_SP_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_8BIT\_SP\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_8BIT_SP__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_16BIT_SP_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_16BIT\_SP\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_16BIT_SP__"
The stack pointer (\s-1SP\s0) register is treated as 8-bit respectively
16-bit register by the compiler.
The definition of these macros is affected by **-mtiny-stack**.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_SPH_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_SPH\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_SPH__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_SP8_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_SP8\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_SP8__"
The device has the \s-1SPH\s0 (high part of stack pointer) special function
register or has an 8-bit stack pointer, respectively.
The definition of these macros is affected by **-mmcu=** and
in the cases of **-mmcu=avr2** and **-mmcu=avr25** also
by **-msp8**.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_RAMPD_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_RAMPD\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_RAMPD__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_RAMPX_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_RAMPX\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_RAMPX__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_RAMPY_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_RAMPY\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_RAMPY__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_HAVE_RAMPZ_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_RAMPZ\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_HAVE_RAMPZ__"
The device has the \f(CW`RAMPD\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPX\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`RAMPY\*(C',
\f(CW`RAMPZ\*(C' special function register, respectively.
.ie n .IP """_\|_NO_INTERRUPTS_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_NO\_INTERRUPTS\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__NO_INTERRUPTS__"
This macro reflects the **-mno-interrupts** command-line option.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_ERRATA_SKIP_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_ERRATA\_SKIP\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_ERRATA_SKIP__"
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_ERRATA_SKIP_JMP_CALL_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_ERRATA\_SKIP\_JMP\_CALL\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_ERRATA_SKIP_JMP_CALL__"
Some \s-1AVR\s0 devices (\s-1AT90S8515,\s0 ATmega103) must not skip 32-bit
instructions because of a hardware erratum.  Skip instructions are
\f(CW`SBRS\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`SBRC\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`SBIS\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`SBIC\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`CPSE\*(C'.
The second macro is only defined if \f(CW`\_\|\_AVR\_HAVE\_JMP\_CALL\_\|\_\*(C' is also
set.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_ISA_RMW_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_ISA\_RMW\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_ISA_RMW__"
The device has Read-Modify-Write instructions (\s-1XCH, LAC, LAS\s0 and \s-1LAT\s0).
.ie n .IP """\_\|\_AVR\_SFR\_OFFSET\_\|\_=_offset_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_SFR\_OFFSET\_\|\_=\f(CIoffset\f(CW" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_SFR_OFFSET__=offset"
Instructions that can address I/O special function registers directly
like \f(CW`IN\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`OUT\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`SBI\*(C', etc. may use a different
address as if addressed by an instruction to access \s-1RAM\s0 like \f(CW`LD\*(C'
or \f(CW`STS\*(C'. This offset depends on the device architecture and has
to be subtracted from the \s-1RAM\s0 address in order to get the
respective I/O@tie{}address.
.ie n .IP """_\|_AVR_SHORT_CALLS_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_SHORT\_CALLS\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_SHORT_CALLS__"
The **-mshort-calls** command line option is set.
.ie n .IP """\_\|\_AVR\_PM\_BASE\_ADDRESS\_\|\_=_addr_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_AVR\_PM\_BASE\_ADDRESS\_\|\_=\f(CIaddr\f(CW" 4
.IX Item "__AVR_PM_BASE_ADDRESS__=addr"
Some devices support reading from flash memory by means of \f(CW`LD*\*(C'
instructions.  The flash memory is seen in the data address space
at an offset of \f(CW`\_\|\_AVR\_PM\_BASE\_ADDRESS\_\|\_\*(C'.  If this macro
is not defined, this feature is not available.  If defined,
the address space is linear and there is no need to put
\f(CW`.rodata\*(C' into \s-1RAM.\s0  This is handled by the default linker
description file, and is currently available for
\f(CW`avrtiny\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`avrxmega3\*(C'.  Even more convenient,
there is no need to use address spaces like \f(CW`\_\|\_flash\*(C' or
features like attribute \f(CW`progmem\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`pgm\_read\_*\*(C'.
.ie n .IP """_\|_WITH_AVRLIBC_\|_""" 4
.el .IP "\f(CW\_\|\_WITH\_AVRLIBC\_\|\_" 4
.IX Item "__WITH_AVRLIBC__"
The compiler is configured to be used together with AVR-Libc.
See the **--with-avrlibc** configure option.

<a name="blackfin-options"></a>

### Blackfin Options

.IX Subsection "Blackfin Options"

* **-mcpu=**_cpu_[**-**_sirevision_]  
  .IX Item "-mcpu=cpu[-sirevision]"
  Specifies the name of the target Blackfin processor.  Currently, _cpu_
  can be one of **bf512**, **bf514**, **bf516**, **bf518**,
  **bf522**, **bf523**, **bf524**, **bf525**, **bf526**,
  **bf527**, **bf531**, **bf532**, **bf533**,
  **bf534**, **bf536**, **bf537**, **bf538**, **bf539**,
  **bf542**, **bf544**, **bf547**, **bf548**, **bf549**,
  **bf542m**, **bf544m**, **bf547m**, **bf548m**, **bf549m**,
  **bf561**, **bf592**.
  .Sp
  The optional _sirevision_ specifies the silicon revision of the target
  Blackfin processor.  Any workarounds available for the targeted silicon revision
  are enabled.  If _sirevision_ is **none**, no workarounds are enabled.
  If _sirevision_ is **any**, all workarounds for the targeted processor
  are enabled.  The \f(CW`\_\|\_SILICON\_REVISION\_\|\_\*(C' macro is defined to two
  hexadecimal digits representing the major and minor numbers in the silicon
  revision.  If _sirevision_ is **none**, the \f(CW`\_\|\_SILICON\_REVISION\_\|\_\*(C'
  is not defined.  If _sirevision_ is **any**, the
  \f(CW`\_\|\_SILICON\_REVISION\_\|\_\*(C' is defined to be \f(CW0xffff.
  If this optional _sirevision_ is not used, \s-1GCC\s0 assumes the latest known
  silicon revision of the targeted Blackfin processor.
  .Sp
  \s-1GCC\s0 defines a preprocessor macro for the specified _cpu_.
  For the **bfin-elf** toolchain, this option causes the hardware \s-1BSP\s0
  provided by libgloss to be linked in if **-msim** is not given.
  .Sp
  Without this option, **bf532** is used as the processor by default.
  .Sp
  Note that support for **bf561** is incomplete.  For **bf561**,
  only the preprocessor macro is defined.
* **-msim**  
  .IX Item "-msim"
  Specifies that the program will be run on the simulator.  This causes
  the simulator \s-1BSP\s0 provided by libgloss to be linked in.  This option
  has effect only for **bfin-elf** toolchain.
  Certain other options, such as **-mid-shared-library** and
  **-mfdpic**, imply **-msim**.
* **-momit-leaf-frame-pointer**  
  .IX Item "-momit-leaf-frame-pointer"
  Don't keep the frame pointer in a register for leaf functions.  This
  avoids the instructions to save, set up and restore frame pointers and
  makes an extra register available in leaf functions.
* **-mspecld-anomaly**  
  .IX Item "-mspecld-anomaly"
  When enabled, the compiler ensures that the generated code does not
  contain speculative loads after jump instructions. If this option is used,
  \f(CW`\_\|\_WORKAROUND\_SPECULATIVE\_LOADS\*(C' is defined.
* **-mno-specld-anomaly**  
  .IX Item "-mno-specld-anomaly"
  Don't generate extra code to prevent speculative loads from occurring.
* **-mcsync-anomaly**  
  .IX Item "-mcsync-anomaly"
  When enabled, the compiler ensures that the generated code does not
  contain \s-1CSYNC\s0 or \s-1SSYNC\s0 instructions too soon after conditional branches.
  If this option is used, \f(CW`\_\|\_WORKAROUND\_SPECULATIVE\_SYNCS\*(C' is defined.
* **-mno-csync-anomaly**  
  .IX Item "-mno-csync-anomaly"
  Don't generate extra code to prevent \s-1CSYNC\s0 or \s-1SSYNC\s0 instructions from
  occurring too soon after a conditional branch.
* **-mlow64k**  
  .IX Item "-mlow64k"
  When enabled, the compiler is free to take advantage of the knowledge that
  the entire program fits into the low 64k of memory.
* **-mno-low64k**  
  .IX Item "-mno-low64k"
  Assume that the program is arbitrarily large.  This is the default.
* **-mstack-check-l1**  
  .IX Item "-mstack-check-l1"
  Do stack checking using information placed into L1 scratchpad memory by the
  uClinux kernel.
* **-mid-shared-library**  
  .IX Item "-mid-shared-library"
  Generate code that supports shared libraries via the library \s-1ID\s0 method.
  This allows for execute in place and shared libraries in an environment
  without virtual memory management.  This option implies **-fPIC**.
  With a **bfin-elf** target, this option implies **-msim**.
* **-mno-id-shared-library**  
  .IX Item "-mno-id-shared-library"
  Generate code that doesn't assume ID-based shared libraries are being used.
  This is the default.
* **-mleaf-id-shared-library**  
  .IX Item "-mleaf-id-shared-library"
  Generate code that supports shared libraries via the library \s-1ID\s0 method,
  but assumes that this library or executable won't link against any other
  \s-1ID\s0 shared libraries.  That allows the compiler to use faster code for jumps
  and calls.
* **-mno-leaf-id-shared-library**  
  .IX Item "-mno-leaf-id-shared-library"
  Do not assume that the code being compiled won't link against any \s-1ID\s0 shared
  libraries.  Slower code is generated for jump and call insns.
* **-mshared-library-id=n**  
  .IX Item "-mshared-library-id=n"
  Specifies the identification number of the ID-based shared library being
  compiled.  Specifying a value of 0 generates more compact code; specifying
  other values forces the allocation of that number to the current
  library but is no more space- or time-efficient than omitting this option.
* **-msep-data**  
  .IX Item "-msep-data"
  Generate code that allows the data segment to be located in a different
  area of memory from the text segment.  This allows for execute in place in
  an environment without virtual memory management by eliminating relocations
  against the text section.
* **-mno-sep-data**  
  .IX Item "-mno-sep-data"
  Generate code that assumes that the data segment follows the text segment.
  This is the default.
* **-mlong-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mlong-calls"
* **-mno-long-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mno-long-calls"
  Tells the compiler to perform function calls by first loading the
  address of the function into a register and then performing a subroutine
  call on this register.  This switch is needed if the target function
  lies outside of the 24-bit addressing range of the offset-based
  version of subroutine call instruction.
  .Sp
  This feature is not enabled by default.  Specifying
  **-mno-long-calls** restores the default behavior.  Note these
  switches have no effect on how the compiler generates code to handle
  function calls via function pointers.
* **-mfast-fp**  
  .IX Item "-mfast-fp"
  Link with the fast floating-point library. This library relaxes some of
  the \s-1IEEE\s0 floating-point standard's rules for checking inputs against
  Not-a-Number (\s-1NAN\s0), in the interest of performance.
* **-minline-plt**  
  .IX Item "-minline-plt"
  Enable inlining of \s-1PLT\s0 entries in function calls to functions that are
  not known to bind locally.  It has no effect without **-mfdpic**.
* **-mmulticore**  
  .IX Item "-mmulticore"
  Build a standalone application for multicore Blackfin processors. 
  This option causes proper start files and link scripts supporting 
  multicore to be used, and defines the macro \f(CW`\_\|\_BFIN\_MULTICORE\*(C'. 
  It can only be used with **-mcpu=bf561**[**-**_sirevision_].
  .Sp
  This option can be used with **-mcorea** or **-mcoreb**, which
  selects the one-application-per-core programming model.  Without
  **-mcorea** or **-mcoreb**, the single-application/dual-core
  programming model is used. In this model, the main function of Core B
  should be named as \f(CW`coreb\_main\*(C'.
  .Sp
  If this option is not used, the single-core application programming
  model is used.
* **-mcorea**  
  .IX Item "-mcorea"
  Build a standalone application for Core A of \s-1BF561\s0 when using
  the one-application-per-core programming model. Proper start files
  and link scripts are used to support Core A, and the macro
  \f(CW`\_\|\_BFIN\_COREA\*(C' is defined.
  This option can only be used in conjunction with **-mmulticore**.
* **-mcoreb**  
  .IX Item "-mcoreb"
  Build a standalone application for Core B of \s-1BF561\s0 when using
  the one-application-per-core programming model. Proper start files
  and link scripts are used to support Core B, and the macro
  \f(CW`\_\|\_BFIN\_COREB\*(C' is defined. When this option is used, \f(CW\*(C\`coreb\_main\*(C'
  should be used instead of \f(CW`main\*(C'. 
  This option can only be used in conjunction with **-mmulticore**.
* **-msdram**  
  .IX Item "-msdram"
  Build a standalone application for \s-1SDRAM.\s0 Proper start files and
  link scripts are used to put the application into \s-1SDRAM,\s0 and the macro
  \f(CW`\_\|\_BFIN\_SDRAM\*(C' is defined.
  The loader should initialize \s-1SDRAM\s0 before loading the application.
* **-micplb**  
  .IX Item "-micplb"
  Assume that ICPLBs are enabled at run time.  This has an effect on certain
  anomaly workarounds.  For Linux targets, the default is to assume ICPLBs
  are enabled; for standalone applications the default is off.

<a name="c6x-options"></a>

### C6X Options

.IX Subsection "C6X Options"

* **-march=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-march=name"
  This specifies the name of the target architecture.  \s-1GCC\s0 uses this
  name to determine what kind of instructions it can emit when generating
  assembly code.  Permissible names are: **c62x**,
  **c64x**, **c64x+**, **c67x**, **c67x+**, **c674x**.
* **-mbig-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mbig-endian"
  Generate code for a big-endian target.
* **-mlittle-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mlittle-endian"
  Generate code for a little-endian target.  This is the default.
* **-msim**  
  .IX Item "-msim"
  Choose startup files and linker script suitable for the simulator.
* **-msdata=default**  
  .IX Item "-msdata=default"
  Put small global and static data in the \f(CW`.neardata\*(C' section,
  which is pointed to by register \f(CW`B14\*(C'.  Put small uninitialized
  global and static data in the \f(CW`.bss\*(C' section, which is adjacent
  to the \f(CW`.neardata\*(C' section.  Put small read-only data into the
  \f(CW`.rodata\*(C' section.  The corresponding sections used for large
  pieces of data are \f(CW`.fardata\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`.far\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`.const\*(C'.
* **-msdata=all**  
  .IX Item "-msdata=all"
  Put all data, not just small objects, into the sections reserved for
  small data, and use addressing relative to the \f(CW`B14\*(C' register to
  access them.
* **-msdata=none**  
  .IX Item "-msdata=none"
  Make no use of the sections reserved for small data, and use absolute
  addresses to access all data.  Put all initialized global and static
  data in the \f(CW`.fardata\*(C' section, and all uninitialized data in the
  \f(CW`.far\*(C' section.  Put all constant data into the \f(CW\*(C\`.const\*(C'
  section.

<a name="s-1criss0-options"></a>

### \s-1CRIS\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "CRIS Options"
These options are defined specifically for the \s-1CRIS\s0 ports.

* **-march=**_architecture-type_  
  .IX Item "-march=architecture-type"
* **-mcpu=**_architecture-type_  
  .IX Item "-mcpu=architecture-type"
  Generate code for the specified architecture.  The choices for
  _architecture-type_ are **v3**, **v8** and **v10** for
  respectively \s-1ETRAX\s0&nbsp;4, \s-1ETRAX\s0&nbsp;100, and \s-1ETRAX\s0&nbsp;100&nbsp;\s-1LX.\s0
  Default is **v0** except for cris-axis-linux-gnu, where the default is
  **v10**.
* **-mtune=**_architecture-type_  
  .IX Item "-mtune=architecture-type"
  Tune to _architecture-type_ everything applicable about the generated
  code, except for the \s-1ABI\s0 and the set of available instructions.  The
  choices for _architecture-type_ are the same as for
  **-march=**_architecture-type_.
* **-mmax-stack-frame=**_n_  
  .IX Item "-mmax-stack-frame=n"
  Warn when the stack frame of a function exceeds _n_ bytes.
* **-metrax4**  
  .IX Item "-metrax4"
* **-metrax100**  
  .IX Item "-metrax100"
  The options **-metrax4** and **-metrax100** are synonyms for
  **-march=v3** and **-march=v8** respectively.
* **-mmul-bug-workaround**  
  .IX Item "-mmul-bug-workaround"
* **-mno-mul-bug-workaround**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mul-bug-workaround"
  Work around a bug in the \f(CW`muls\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`mulu\*(C' instructions for \s-1CPU\s0
  models where it applies.  This option is active by default.
* **-mpdebug**  
  .IX Item "-mpdebug"
  Enable CRIS-specific verbose debug-related information in the assembly
  code.  This option also has the effect of turning off the **#NO\_APP**
  formatted-code indicator to the assembler at the beginning of the
  assembly file.
* **-mcc-init**  
  .IX Item "-mcc-init"
  Do not use condition-code results from previous instruction; always emit
  compare and test instructions before use of condition codes.
* **-mno-side-effects**  
  .IX Item "-mno-side-effects"
  Do not emit instructions with side effects in addressing modes other than
  post-increment.
* **-mstack-align**  
  .IX Item "-mstack-align"
* **-mno-stack-align**  
  .IX Item "-mno-stack-align"
* **-mdata-align**  
  .IX Item "-mdata-align"
* **-mno-data-align**  
  .IX Item "-mno-data-align"
* **-mconst-align**  
  .IX Item "-mconst-align"
* **-mno-const-align**  
  .IX Item "-mno-const-align"
  These options (**no-** options) arrange (eliminate arrangements) for the
  stack frame, individual data and constants to be aligned for the maximum
  single data access size for the chosen \s-1CPU\s0 model.  The default is to
  arrange for 32-bit alignment.  \s-1ABI\s0 details such as structure layout are
  not affected by these options.
* **-m32-bit**  
  .IX Item "-m32-bit"
* **-m16-bit**  
  .IX Item "-m16-bit"
* **-m8-bit**  
  .IX Item "-m8-bit"
  Similar to the stack- data- and const-align options above, these options
  arrange for stack frame, writable data and constants to all be 32-bit,
  16-bit or 8-bit aligned.  The default is 32-bit alignment.
* **-mno-prologue-epilogue**  
  .IX Item "-mno-prologue-epilogue"
* **-mprologue-epilogue**  
  .IX Item "-mprologue-epilogue"
  With **-mno-prologue-epilogue**, the normal function prologue and
  epilogue which set up the stack frame are omitted and no return
  instructions or return sequences are generated in the code.  Use this
  option only together with visual inspection of the compiled code: no
  warnings or errors are generated when call-saved registers must be saved,
  or storage for local variables needs to be allocated.
* **-mno-gotplt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-gotplt"
* **-mgotplt**  
  .IX Item "-mgotplt"
  With **-fpic** and **-fPIC**, don't generate (do generate)
  instruction sequences that load addresses for functions from the \s-1PLT\s0 part
  of the \s-1GOT\s0 rather than (traditional on other architectures) calls to the
  \s-1PLT.\s0  The default is **-mgotplt**.
* **-melf**  
  .IX Item "-melf"
  Legacy no-op option only recognized with the cris-axis-elf and
  cris-axis-linux-gnu targets.
* **-mlinux**  
  .IX Item "-mlinux"
  Legacy no-op option only recognized with the cris-axis-linux-gnu target.
* **-sim**  
  .IX Item "-sim"
  This option, recognized for the cris-axis-elf, arranges
  to link with input-output functions from a simulator library.  Code,
  initialized data and zero-initialized data are allocated consecutively.
* **-sim2**  
  .IX Item "-sim2"
  Like **-sim**, but pass linker options to locate initialized data at
  0x40000000 and zero-initialized data at 0x80000000.

<a name="s-1cr16s0-options"></a>

### \s-1CR16\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "CR16 Options"
These options are defined specifically for the \s-1CR16\s0 ports.

* **-mmac**  
  .IX Item "-mmac"
  Enable the use of multiply-accumulate instructions. Disabled by default.
* **-mcr16cplus**  
  .IX Item "-mcr16cplus"
* **-mcr16c**  
  .IX Item "-mcr16c"
  Generate code for \s-1CR16C\s0 or \s-1CR16C+\s0 architecture. \s-1CR16C+\s0 architecture 
  is default.
* **-msim**  
  .IX Item "-msim"
  Links the library libsim.a which is in compatible with simulator. Applicable
  to \s-1ELF\s0 compiler only.
* **-mint32**  
  .IX Item "-mint32"
  Choose integer type as 32-bit wide.
* **-mbit-ops**  
  .IX Item "-mbit-ops"
  Generates \f(CW`sbit\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`cbit\*(C' instructions for bit manipulations.
* **-mdata-model=**_model_  
  .IX Item "-mdata-model=model"
  Choose a data model. The choices for _model_ are **near**,
  **far** or **medium**. **medium** is default.
  However, **far** is not valid with **-mcr16c**, as the
  \s-1CR16C\s0 architecture does not support the far data model.

<a name="c-sky-options"></a>

### C\-SKY Options

.IX Subsection "C-SKY Options"
\s-1GCC\s0 supports these options when compiling for C-SKY V2 processors.

* **-march=**_arch_  
  .IX Item "-march=arch"
  Specify the C-SKY target architecture.  Valid values for _arch_ are:
  **ck801**, **ck802**, **ck803**, **ck807**, and **ck810**.
  The default is **ck810**.
* **-mcpu=**_cpu_  
  .IX Item "-mcpu=cpu"
  Specify the C-SKY target processor.  Valid values for _cpu_ are:
  **ck801**, **ck801t**,
  **ck802**, **ck802t**, **ck802j**,
  **ck803**, **ck803h**, **ck803t**, **ck803ht**,
  **ck803f**, **ck803fh**, **ck803e**, **ck803eh**,
  **ck803et**, **ck803eht**, **ck803ef**, **ck803efh**,
  **ck803ft**, **ck803eft**, **ck803efht**, **ck803r1**,
  **ck803hr1**, **ck803tr1**, **ck803htr1**, **ck803fr1**,
  **ck803fhr1**, **ck803er1**, **ck803ehr1**, **ck803etr1**,
  **ck803ehtr1**, **ck803efr1**, **ck803efhr1**, **ck803ftr1**,
  **ck803eftr1**, **ck803efhtr1**,
  **ck803s**, **ck803st**, **ck803se**, **ck803sf**,
  **ck803sef**, **ck803seft**,
  **ck807e**, **ck807ef**, **ck807**, **ck807f**,
  **ck810e**, **ck810et**, **ck810ef**, **ck810eft**,
  **ck810**, **ck810v**, **ck810f**, **ck810t**, **ck810fv**,
  **ck810tv**, **ck810ft**, and **ck810ftv**.
* **-mbig-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mbig-endian"
* **-EB**  
  .IX Item "-EB"
* **-mlittle-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mlittle-endian"
* **-EL**  
  .IX Item "-EL"
  Select big- or little-endian code.  The default is little-endian.
* **-mhard-float**  
  .IX Item "-mhard-float"
* **-msoft-float**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-float"
  Select hardware or software floating-point implementations.
  The default is soft float.
* **-mdouble-float**  
  .IX Item "-mdouble-float"
* **-mno-double-float**  
  .IX Item "-mno-double-float"
  When **-mhard-float** is in effect, enable generation of
  double-precision float instructions.  This is the default except
  when compiling for \s-1CK803.\s0
* **-mfdivdu**  
  .IX Item "-mfdivdu"
* **-mno-fdivdu**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fdivdu"
  When **-mhard-float** is in effect, enable generation of
  \f(CW`frecipd\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`fsqrtd\*(C', and \f(CW\*(C\`fdivd\*(C' instructions.
  This is the default except when compiling for \s-1CK803.\s0
* **-mfpu=**_fpu_  
  .IX Item "-mfpu=fpu"
  Select the floating-point processor.  This option can only be used with
  **-mhard-float**.
  Values for _fpu_ are
  **fpv2\_sf** (equivalent to **-mno-double-float -mno-fdivdu**),
  **fpv2** (**-mdouble-float -mno-divdu**), and
  **fpv2\_divd** (**-mdouble-float -mdivdu**).
* **-melrw**  
  .IX Item "-melrw"
* **-mno-elrw**  
  .IX Item "-mno-elrw"
  Enable the extended \f(CW`lrw\*(C' instruction.  This option defaults to on
  for \s-1CK801\s0 and off otherwise.
* **-mistack**  
  .IX Item "-mistack"
* **-mno-istack**  
  .IX Item "-mno-istack"
  Enable interrupt stack instructions; the default is off.
  .Sp
  The **-mistack** option is required to handle the
  \f(CW`interrupt\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`isr\*(C' function attributes.
* **-mmp**  
  .IX Item "-mmp"
  Enable multiprocessor instructions; the default is off.
* **-mcp**  
  .IX Item "-mcp"
  Enable coprocessor instructions; the default is off.
* **-mcache**  
  .IX Item "-mcache"
  Enable coprocessor instructions; the default is off.
* **-msecurity**  
  .IX Item "-msecurity"
  Enable C-SKY security instructions; the default is off.
* **-mtrust**  
  .IX Item "-mtrust"
  Enable C-SKY trust instructions; the default is off.
* **-mdsp**  
  .IX Item "-mdsp"
* **-medsp**  
  .IX Item "-medsp"
* **-mvdsp**  
  .IX Item "-mvdsp"
  Enable C-SKY \s-1DSP,\s0 Enhanced \s-1DSP,\s0 or Vector \s-1DSP\s0 instructions, respectively.
  All of these options default to off.
* **-mdiv**  
  .IX Item "-mdiv"
* **-mno-div**  
  .IX Item "-mno-div"
  Generate divide instructions.  Default is off.
* **-msmart**  
  .IX Item "-msmart"
* **-mno-smart**  
  .IX Item "-mno-smart"
  Generate code for Smart Mode, using only registers numbered 0-7 to allow
  use of 16-bit instructions.  This option is ignored for \s-1CK801\s0 where this
  is the required behavior, and it defaults to on for \s-1CK802.\s0
  For other targets, the default is off.
* **-mhigh-registers**  
  .IX Item "-mhigh-registers"
* **-mno-high-registers**  
  .IX Item "-mno-high-registers"
  Generate code using the high registers numbered 16-31.  This option
  is not supported on \s-1CK801, CK802,\s0 or \s-1CK803,\s0 and is enabled by default
  for other processors.
* **-manchor**  
  .IX Item "-manchor"
* **-mno-anchor**  
  .IX Item "-mno-anchor"
  Generate code using global anchor symbol addresses.
* **-mpushpop**  
  .IX Item "-mpushpop"
* **-mno-pushpop**  
  .IX Item "-mno-pushpop"
  Generate code using \f(CW`push\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`pop\*(C' instructions.  This option
  defaults to on.
* **-mmultiple-stld**  
  .IX Item "-mmultiple-stld"
* **-mstm**  
  .IX Item "-mstm"
* **-mno-multiple-stld**  
  .IX Item "-mno-multiple-stld"
* **-mno-stm**  
  .IX Item "-mno-stm"
  Generate code using \f(CW`stm\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`ldm\*(C' instructions.  This option
  isn't supported on \s-1CK801\s0 but is enabled by default on other processors.
* **-mconstpool**  
  .IX Item "-mconstpool"
* **-mno-constpool**  
  .IX Item "-mno-constpool"
  Create constant pools in the compiler instead of deferring it to the
  assembler.  This option is the default and required for correct code
  generation on \s-1CK801\s0 and \s-1CK802,\s0 and is optional on other processors.
* **-mstack-size**  
  .IX Item "-mstack-size"
* **-mno-stack-size**  
  .IX Item "-mno-stack-size"
  Emit \f(CW`.stack\_size\*(C' directives for each function in the assembly
  output.  This option defaults to off.
* **-mccrt**  
  .IX Item "-mccrt"
* **-mno-ccrt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ccrt"
  Generate code for the C-SKY compiler runtime instead of libgcc.  This
  option defaults to off.
* **-mbranch-cost=**_n_  
  .IX Item "-mbranch-cost=n"
  Set the branch costs to roughly \f(CW`n\*(C' instructions.  The default is 1.
* **-msched-prolog**  
  .IX Item "-msched-prolog"
* **-mno-sched-prolog**  
  .IX Item "-mno-sched-prolog"
  Permit scheduling of function prologue and epilogue sequences.  Using
  this option can result in code that is not compliant with the C-SKY V2 \s-1ABI\s0
  prologue requirements and that cannot be debugged or backtraced.
  It is disabled by default.

<a name="darwin-options"></a>

### Darwin Options

.IX Subsection "Darwin Options"
These options are defined for all architectures running the Darwin operating
system.

\s-1FSF GCC\s0 on Darwin does not create fat\*(R" object files; it creates
an object file for the single architecture that \s-1GCC\s0 was built to
target.  Apple's \s-1GCC\s0 on Darwin does create fat\*(R" files if multiple
**-arch** options are used; it does so by running the compiler or
linker multiple times and joining the results together with
_lipo_.

The subtype of the file created (like **ppc7400** or **ppc970** or
**i686**) is determined by the flags that specify the \s-1ISA\s0
that \s-1GCC\s0 is targeting, like **-mcpu** or **-march**.  The
**-force\_cpusubtype\_ALL** option can be used to override this.

The Darwin tools vary in their behavior when presented with an \s-1ISA\s0
mismatch.  The assembler, _as_, only permits instructions to
be used that are valid for the subtype of the file it is generating,
so you cannot put 64-bit instructions in a **ppc750** object file.
The linker for shared libraries, _/usr/bin/libtool_, fails
and prints an error if asked to create a shared library with a less
restrictive subtype than its input files (for instance, trying to put
a **ppc970** object file in a **ppc7400** library).  The linker
for executables, **ld**, quietly gives the executable the most
restrictive subtype of any of its input files.

* **-F**_dir_  
  .IX Item "-Fdir"
  Add the framework directory _dir_ to the head of the list of
  directories to be searched for header files.  These directories are
  interleaved with those specified by **-I** options and are
  scanned in a left-to-right order.
  .Sp
  A framework directory is a directory with frameworks in it.  A
  framework is a directory with a _Headers_ and/or
  _PrivateHeaders_ directory contained directly in it that ends
  in _.framework_.  The name of a framework is the name of this
  directory excluding the _.framework_.  Headers associated with
  the framework are found in one of those two directories, with
  _Headers_ being searched first.  A subframework is a framework
  directory that is in a framework's _Frameworks_ directory.
  Includes of subframework headers can only appear in a header of a
  framework that contains the subframework, or in a sibling subframework
  header.  Two subframeworks are siblings if they occur in the same
  framework.  A subframework should not have the same name as a
  framework; a warning is issued if this is violated.  Currently a
  subframework cannot have subframeworks; in the future, the mechanism
  may be extended to support this.  The standard frameworks can be found
  in _/System/Library/Frameworks_ and
  _/Library/Frameworks_.  An example include looks like
  \f(CW`#include &lt;Framework/header.h&gt;\*(C', where _Framework_ denotes
  the name of the framework and _header.h_ is found in the
  _PrivateHeaders_ or _Headers_ directory.
* **-iframework**_dir_  
  .IX Item "-iframeworkdir"
  Like **-F** except the directory is a treated as a system
  directory.  The main difference between this **-iframework** and
  **-F** is that with **-iframework** the compiler does not
  warn about constructs contained within header files found via
  _dir_.  This option is valid only for the C family of languages.
* **-gused**  
  .IX Item "-gused"
  Emit debugging information for symbols that are used.  For stabs
  debugging format, this enables **-feliminate-unused-debug-symbols**.
  This is by default \s-1ON.\s0
* **-gfull**  
  .IX Item "-gfull"
  Emit debugging information for all symbols and types.
* **-mmacosx-version-min=**_version_  
  .IX Item "-mmacosx-version-min=version"
  The earliest version of MacOS X that this executable will run on
  is _version_.  Typical values of _version_ include \f(CW10.1,
  \f(CW10.2, and \f(CW10.3.9.
  .Sp
  If the compiler was built to use the system's headers by default,
  then the default for this option is the system version on which the
  compiler is running, otherwise the default is to make choices that
  are compatible with as many systems and code bases as possible.
* **-mkernel**  
  .IX Item "-mkernel"
  Enable kernel development mode.  The **-mkernel** option sets
  **-static**, **-fno-common**, **-fno-use-cxa-atexit**,
  **-fno-exceptions**, **-fno-non-call-exceptions**,
  **-fapple-kext**, **-fno-weak** and **-fno-rtti** where
  applicable.  This mode also sets **-mno-altivec**,
  **-msoft-float**, **-fno-builtin** and
  **-mlong-branch** for PowerPC targets.
* **-mone-byte-bool**  
  .IX Item "-mone-byte-bool"
  Override the defaults for \f(CW`bool\*(C' so that \f(CW\*(C\`sizeof(bool)==1\*(C'.
  By default \f(CW`sizeof(bool)\*(C' is \f(CW4 when compiling for
  Darwin/PowerPC and \f(CW1 when compiling for Darwin/x86, so this
  option has no effect on x86.
  .Sp
  **Warning:** The **-mone-byte-bool** switch causes \s-1GCC\s0
  to generate code that is not binary compatible with code generated
  without that switch.  Using this switch may require recompiling all
  other modules in a program, including system libraries.  Use this
  switch to conform to a non-default data model.
* **-mfix-and-continue**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-and-continue"
* **-ffix-and-continue**  
  .IX Item "-ffix-and-continue"
* **-findirect-data**  
  .IX Item "-findirect-data"
  Generate code suitable for fast turnaround development, such as to
  allow \s-1GDB\s0 to dynamically load _.o_ files into already-running
  programs.  **-findirect-data** and **-ffix-and-continue**
  are provided for backwards compatibility.
* **-all\_load**  
  .IX Item "-all_load"
  Loads all members of static archive libraries.
  See man **ld**\|(1) for more information.
* **-arch\_errors\_fatal**  
  .IX Item "-arch_errors_fatal"
  Cause the errors having to do with files that have the wrong architecture
  to be fatal.
* **-bind\_at\_load**  
  .IX Item "-bind_at_load"
  Causes the output file to be marked such that the dynamic linker will
  bind all undefined references when the file is loaded or launched.
* **-bundle**  
  .IX Item "-bundle"
  Produce a Mach-o bundle format file.
  See man **ld**\|(1) for more information.
* **-bundle\_loader** _executable_  
  .IX Item "-bundle_loader executable"
  This option specifies the _executable_ that will load the build
  output file being linked.  See man **ld**\|(1) for more information.
* **-dynamiclib**  
  .IX Item "-dynamiclib"
  When passed this option, \s-1GCC\s0 produces a dynamic library instead of
  an executable when linking, using the Darwin _libtool_ command.
* **-force\_cpusubtype\_ALL**  
  .IX Item "-force_cpusubtype_ALL"
  This causes \s-1GCC\s0's output file to have the **\s-1ALL\s0** subtype, instead of
  one controlled by the **-mcpu** or **-march** option.
* **-allowable\_client**  _client\_name_  
  .IX Item "-allowable_client client_name"
* **-client\_name**  
  .IX Item "-client_name"
* **-compatibility\_version**  
  .IX Item "-compatibility_version"
* **-current\_version**  
  .IX Item "-current_version"
* **-dead\_strip**  
  .IX Item "-dead_strip"
* **-dependency-file**  
  .IX Item "-dependency-file"
* **-dylib\_file**  
  .IX Item "-dylib_file"
* **-dylinker\_install\_name**  
  .IX Item "-dylinker_install_name"
* **-dynamic**  
  .IX Item "-dynamic"
* **-exported\_symbols\_list**  
  .IX Item "-exported_symbols_list"
* **-filelist**  
  .IX Item "-filelist"
* **-flat\_namespace**  
  .IX Item "-flat_namespace"
* **-force\_flat\_namespace**  
  .IX Item "-force_flat_namespace"
* **-headerpad\_max\_install\_names**  
  .IX Item "-headerpad_max_install_names"
* **-image\_base**  
  .IX Item "-image_base"
* **-init**  
  .IX Item "-init"
* **-install\_name**  
  .IX Item "-install_name"
* **-keep\_private\_externs**  
  .IX Item "-keep_private_externs"
* **-multi\_module**  
  .IX Item "-multi_module"
* **-multiply\_defined**  
  .IX Item "-multiply_defined"
* **-multiply\_defined\_unused**
