  Use the hardware barrel shifter.
* **-mxl-pattern-compare**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-pattern-compare"
  Use pattern compare instructions.
* **-msmall-divides**  
  .IX Item "-msmall-divides"
  Use table lookup optimization for small signed integer divisions.
* **-mxl-stack-check**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-stack-check"
  This option is deprecated.  Use **-fstack-check** instead.
* **-mxl-gp-opt**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-gp-opt"
  Use GP-relative \f(CW`.sdata\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`.sbss\*(C' sections.
* **-mxl-multiply-high**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-multiply-high"
  Use multiply high instructions for high part of 32x32 multiply.
* **-mxl-float-convert**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-float-convert"
  Use hardware floating-point conversion instructions.
* **-mxl-float-sqrt**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-float-sqrt"
  Use hardware floating-point square root instruction.
* **-mbig-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mbig-endian"
  Generate code for a big-endian target.
* **-mlittle-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mlittle-endian"
  Generate code for a little-endian target.
* **-mxl-reorder**  
  .IX Item "-mxl-reorder"
  Use reorder instructions (swap and byte reversed load/store).
* **-mxl-mode-**_app-model_  
  .IX Item "-mxl-mode-app-model"
  Select application model _app-model_.  Valid models are
    * **executable**  
      .IX Item "executable"
      normal executable (default), uses startup code _crt0.o_.
    * **-mpic-data-is-text-relative**  
      .IX Item "-mpic-data-is-text-relative"
      Assume that the displacement between the text and data segments is fixed
      at static link time.  This allows data to be referenced by offset from start of
      text address instead of \s-1GOT\s0 since PC-relative addressing is not supported.
    * **xmdstub**  
      .IX Item "xmdstub"
      for use with Xilinx Microprocessor Debugger (\s-1XMD\s0) based
      software intrusive debug agent called xmdstub. This uses startup file
      _crt1.o_ and sets the start address of the program to 0x800.
    * **bootstrap**  
      .IX Item "bootstrap"
      for applications that are loaded using a bootloader.
      This model uses startup file _crt2.o_ which does not contain a processor
      reset vector handler. This is suitable for transferring control on a
      processor reset to the bootloader rather than the application.
    * **novectors**  
      .IX Item "novectors"
      for applications that do not require any of the
      MicroBlaze vectors. This option may be useful for applications running
      within a monitoring application. This model uses _crt3.o_ as a startup file.
      .Sp
      Option **-xl-mode-**_app-model_ is a deprecated alias for
      **-mxl-mode-**_app-model_.

<a name="s-1mipss0-options"></a>

### \s-1MIPS\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "MIPS Options"

* **-EB**  
  .IX Item "-EB"
  Generate big-endian code.
* **-EL**  
  .IX Item "-EL"
  Generate little-endian code.  This is the default for **mips*el-*-***
  configurations.
* **-march=**_arch_  
  .IX Item "-march=arch"
  Generate code that runs on _arch_, which can be the name of a
  generic \s-1MIPS ISA,\s0 or the name of a particular processor.
  The \s-1ISA\s0 names are:
  **mips1**, **mips2**, **mips3**, **mips4**,
  **mips32**, **mips32r2**, **mips32r3**, **mips32r5**,
  **mips32r6**, **mips64**, **mips64r2**, **mips64r3**,
  **mips64r5** and **mips64r6**.
  The processor names are:
  **4kc**, **4km**, **4kp**, **4ksc**,
  **4kec**, **4kem**, **4kep**, **4ksd**,
  **5kc**, **5kf**,
  **20kc**,
  **24kc**, **24kf2\_1**, **24kf1\_1**,
  **24kec**, **24kef2\_1**, **24kef1\_1**,
  **34kc**, **34kf2\_1**, **34kf1\_1**, **34kn**,
  **74kc**, **74kf2\_1**, **74kf1\_1**, **74kf3\_2**,
  **1004kc**, **1004kf2\_1**, **1004kf1\_1**,
  **i6400**, **i6500**,
  **interaptiv**,
  **loongson2e**, **loongson2f**, **loongson3a**, **gs464**,
  **gs464e**, **gs264e**,
  **m4k**,
  **m14k**, **m14kc**, **m14ke**, **m14kec**,
  **m5100**, **m5101**,
  **octeon**, **octeon+**, **octeon2**, **octeon3**,
  **orion**,
  **p5600**, **p6600**,
  **r2000**, **r3000**, **r3900**, **r4000**, **r4400**,
  **r4600**, **r4650**, **r4700**, **r5900**,
  **r6000**, **r8000**,
  **rm7000**, **rm9000**,
  **r10000**, **r12000**, **r14000**, **r16000**,
  **sb1**,
  **sr71000**,
  **vr4100**, **vr4111**, **vr4120**, **vr4130**, **vr4300**,
  **vr5000**, **vr5400**, **vr5500**,
  **xlr** and **xlp**.
  The special value **from-abi** selects the
  most compatible architecture for the selected \s-1ABI\s0 (that is,
  **mips1** for 32-bit ABIs and **mips3** for 64-bit ABIs).
  .Sp
  The native Linux/GNU toolchain also supports the value **native**,
  which selects the best architecture option for the host processor.
  **-march=native** has no effect if \s-1GCC\s0 does not recognize
  the processor.
  .Sp
  In processor names, a final **000** can be abbreviated as **k**
  (for example, **-march=r2k**).  Prefixes are optional, and
  **vr** may be written **r**.
  .Sp
  Names of the form _n_**f2\_1** refer to processors with
  FPUs clocked at half the rate of the core, names of the form
  _n_**f1\_1** refer to processors with FPUs clocked at the same
  rate as the core, and names of the form _n_**f3\_2** refer to
  processors with FPUs clocked a ratio of 3:2 with respect to the core.
  For compatibility reasons, _n_**f** is accepted as a synonym
  for _n_**f2\_1** while _n_**x** and _b_**fx** are
  accepted as synonyms for _n_**f1\_1**.
  .Sp
  \s-1GCC\s0 defines two macros based on the value of this option.  The first
  is \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\*(C', which gives the name of target architecture, as
  a string.  The second has the form \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\_\f(CIfoo\f(CW\*(C',
  where _foo_ is the capitalized value of \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\*(C'.
  For example, **-march=r2000** sets \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\*(C'
  to \f(CW"r2000" and defines the macro \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\_R2000\*(C'.
  .Sp
  Note that the \f(CW`\_MIPS\_ARCH\*(C' macro uses the processor names given
  above.  In other words, it has the full prefix and does not
  abbreviate **000** as **k**.  In the case of **from-abi**,
  the macro names the resolved architecture (either \f(CW"mips1" or
  \f(CW"mips3").  It names the default architecture when no
  **-march** option is given.
* **-mtune=**_arch_  
  .IX Item "-mtune=arch"
  Optimize for _arch_.  Among other things, this option controls
  the way instructions are scheduled, and the perceived cost of arithmetic
  operations.  The list of _arch_ values is the same as for
  **-march**.
  .Sp
  When this option is not used, \s-1GCC\s0 optimizes for the processor
  specified by **-march**.  By using **-march** and
  **-mtune** together, it is possible to generate code that
  runs on a family of processors, but optimize the code for one
  particular member of that family.
  .Sp
  **-mtune** defines the macros \f(CW`\_MIPS\_TUNE\*(C' and
  \f(CW`\_MIPS\_TUNE\_\f(CIfoo\f(CW\*(C', which work in the same way as the
  **-march** ones described above.
* **-mips1**  
  .IX Item "-mips1"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips1**.
* **-mips2**  
  .IX Item "-mips2"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips2**.
* **-mips3**  
  .IX Item "-mips3"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips3**.
* **-mips4**  
  .IX Item "-mips4"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips4**.
* **-mips32**  
  .IX Item "-mips32"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips32**.
* **-mips32r3**  
  .IX Item "-mips32r3"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips32r3**.
* **-mips32r5**  
  .IX Item "-mips32r5"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips32r5**.
* **-mips32r6**  
  .IX Item "-mips32r6"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips32r6**.
* **-mips64**  
  .IX Item "-mips64"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips64**.
* **-mips64r2**  
  .IX Item "-mips64r2"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips64r2**.
* **-mips64r3**  
  .IX Item "-mips64r3"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips64r3**.
* **-mips64r5**  
  .IX Item "-mips64r5"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips64r5**.
* **-mips64r6**  
  .IX Item "-mips64r6"
  Equivalent to **-march=mips64r6**.
* **-mips16**  
  .IX Item "-mips16"
* **-mno-mips16**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mips16"
  Generate (do not generate) \s-1MIPS16\s0 code.  If \s-1GCC\s0 is targeting a
  \s-1MIPS32\s0 or \s-1MIPS64\s0 architecture, it makes use of the MIPS16e \s-1ASE.\s0
  .Sp
  \s-1MIPS16\s0 code generation can also be controlled on a per-function basis
  by means of \f(CW`mips16\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`nomips16\*(C' attributes.
* **-mflip-mips16**  
  .IX Item "-mflip-mips16"
  Generate \s-1MIPS16\s0 code on alternating functions.  This option is provided
  for regression testing of mixed MIPS16/non-MIPS16 code generation, and is
  not intended for ordinary use in compiling user code.
* **-minterlink-compressed**  
  .IX Item "-minterlink-compressed"
* **-mno-interlink-compressed**  
  .IX Item "-mno-interlink-compressed"
  Require (do not require) that code using the standard (uncompressed) \s-1MIPS ISA\s0
  be link-compatible with \s-1MIPS16\s0 and microMIPS code, and vice versa.
  .Sp
  For example, code using the standard \s-1ISA\s0 encoding cannot jump directly
  to \s-1MIPS16\s0 or microMIPS code; it must either use a call or an indirect jump.
  **-minterlink-compressed** therefore disables direct jumps unless \s-1GCC\s0
  knows that the target of the jump is not compressed.
* **-minterlink-mips16**  
  .IX Item "-minterlink-mips16"
* **-mno-interlink-mips16**  
  .IX Item "-mno-interlink-mips16"
  Aliases of **-minterlink-compressed** and
  **-mno-interlink-compressed**.  These options predate the microMIPS \s-1ASE\s0
  and are retained for backwards compatibility.
* **-mabi=32**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=32"
* **-mabi=o64**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=o64"
* **-mabi=n32**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=n32"
* **-mabi=64**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=64"
* **-mabi=eabi**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=eabi"
  Generate code for the given \s-1ABI.\s0
  .Sp
  Note that the \s-1EABI\s0 has a 32-bit and a 64-bit variant.  \s-1GCC\s0 normally
  generates 64-bit code when you select a 64-bit architecture, but you
  can use **-mgp32** to get 32-bit code instead.
  .Sp
  For information about the O64 \s-1ABI,\s0 see
  &lt;**http://gcc.gnu.org/projects/mipso64-abi.html**&gt;.
  .Sp
  \s-1GCC\s0 supports a variant of the o32 \s-1ABI\s0 in which floating-point registers
  are 64 rather than 32 bits wide.  You can select this combination with
  **-mabi=32** **-mfp64**.  This \s-1ABI\s0 relies on the \f(CW`mthc1\*(C'
  and \f(CW`mfhc1\*(C' instructions and is therefore only supported for
  \s-1MIPS32R2, MIPS32R3\s0 and \s-1MIPS32R5\s0 processors.
  .Sp
  The register assignments for arguments and return values remain the
  same, but each scalar value is passed in a single 64-bit register
  rather than a pair of 32-bit registers.  For example, scalar
  floating-point values are returned in **\f(CB$f0** only, not a
  **\f(CB$f0**/**\f(CB$f1** pair.  The set of call-saved registers also
  remains the same in that the even-numbered double-precision registers
  are saved.
  .Sp
  Two additional variants of the o32 \s-1ABI\s0 are supported to enable
  a transition from 32-bit to 64-bit registers.  These are \s-1FPXX\s0
  (**-mfpxx**) and \s-1FP64A\s0 (**-mfp64** **-mno-odd-spreg**).
  The \s-1FPXX\s0 extension mandates that all code must execute correctly
  when run using 32-bit or 64-bit registers.  The code can be interlinked
  with either \s-1FP32\s0 or \s-1FP64,\s0 but not both.
  The \s-1FP64A\s0 extension is similar to the \s-1FP64\s0 extension but forbids the
  use of odd-numbered single-precision registers.  This can be used
  in conjunction with the \f(CW`FRE\*(C' mode of FPUs in \s-1MIPS32R5\s0
  processors and allows both \s-1FP32\s0 and \s-1FP64A\s0 code to interlink and
  run in the same process without changing \s-1FPU\s0 modes.
* **-mabicalls**  
  .IX Item "-mabicalls"
* **-mno-abicalls**  
  .IX Item "-mno-abicalls"
  Generate (do not generate) code that is suitable for SVR4-style
  dynamic objects.  **-mabicalls** is the default for SVR4-based
  systems.
* **-mshared**  
  .IX Item "-mshared"
* **-mno-shared**  
  .IX Item "-mno-shared"
  Generate (do not generate) code that is fully position-independent,
  and that can therefore be linked into shared libraries.  This option
  only affects **-mabicalls**.
  .Sp
  All **-mabicalls** code has traditionally been position-independent,
  regardless of options like **-fPIC** and **-fpic**.  However,
  as an extension, the \s-1GNU\s0 toolchain allows executables to use absolute
  accesses for locally-binding symbols.  It can also use shorter \s-1GP\s0
  initialization sequences and generate direct calls to locally-defined
  functions.  This mode is selected by **-mno-shared**.
  .Sp
  **-mno-shared** depends on binutils 2.16 or higher and generates
  objects that can only be linked by the \s-1GNU\s0 linker.  However, the option
  does not affect the \s-1ABI\s0 of the final executable; it only affects the \s-1ABI\s0
  of relocatable objects.  Using **-mno-shared** generally makes
  executables both smaller and quicker.
  .Sp
  **-mshared** is the default.
* **-mplt**  
  .IX Item "-mplt"
* **-mno-plt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-plt"
  Assume (do not assume) that the static and dynamic linkers
  support PLTs and copy relocations.  This option only affects
  **-mno-shared -mabicalls**.  For the n64 \s-1ABI,\s0 this option
  has no effect without **-msym32**.
  .Sp
  You can make **-mplt** the default by configuring
  \s-1GCC\s0 with **--with-mips-plt**.  The default is
  **-mno-plt** otherwise.
* **-mxgot**  
  .IX Item "-mxgot"
* **-mno-xgot**  
  .IX Item "-mno-xgot"
  Lift (do not lift) the usual restrictions on the size of the global
  offset table.
  .Sp
  \s-1GCC\s0 normally uses a single instruction to load values from the \s-1GOT.\s0
  While this is relatively efficient, it only works if the \s-1GOT\s0
  is smaller than about 64k.  Anything larger causes the linker
  to report an error such as:
  .Sp
  .Vb 1
          relocation truncated to fit: R_MIPS_GOT16 foobar
  .Ve
  .Sp
  If this happens, you should recompile your code with **-mxgot**.
  This works with very large GOTs, although the code is also
  less efficient, since it takes three instructions to fetch the
  value of a global symbol.
  .Sp
  Note that some linkers can create multiple GOTs.  If you have such a
  linker, you should only need to use **-mxgot** when a single object
  file accesses more than 64k's worth of \s-1GOT\s0 entries.  Very few do.
  .Sp
  These options have no effect unless \s-1GCC\s0 is generating position
  independent code.
* **-mgp32**  
  .IX Item "-mgp32"
  Assume that general-purpose registers are 32 bits wide.
* **-mgp64**  
  .IX Item "-mgp64"
  Assume that general-purpose registers are 64 bits wide.
* **-mfp32**  
  .IX Item "-mfp32"
  Assume that floating-point registers are 32 bits wide.
* **-mfp64**  
  .IX Item "-mfp64"
  Assume that floating-point registers are 64 bits wide.
* **-mfpxx**  
  .IX Item "-mfpxx"
  Do not assume the width of floating-point registers.
* **-mhard-float**  
  .IX Item "-mhard-float"
  Use floating-point coprocessor instructions.
* **-msoft-float**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-float"
  Do not use floating-point coprocessor instructions.  Implement
  floating-point calculations using library calls instead.
* **-mno-float**  
  .IX Item "-mno-float"
  Equivalent to **-msoft-float**, but additionally asserts that the
  program being compiled does not perform any floating-point operations.
  This option is presently supported only by some bare-metal \s-1MIPS\s0
  configurations, where it may select a special set of libraries
  that lack all floating-point support (including, for example, the
  floating-point \f(CW`printf\*(C' formats).  
  If code compiled with **-mno-float** accidentally contains
  floating-point operations, it is likely to suffer a link-time
  or run-time failure.
* **-msingle-float**  
  .IX Item "-msingle-float"
  Assume that the floating-point coprocessor only supports single-precision
  operations.
* **-mdouble-float**  
  .IX Item "-mdouble-float"
  Assume that the floating-point coprocessor supports double-precision
  operations.  This is the default.
* **-modd-spreg**  
  .IX Item "-modd-spreg"
* **-mno-odd-spreg**  
  .IX Item "-mno-odd-spreg"
  Enable the use of odd-numbered single-precision floating-point registers
  for the o32 \s-1ABI.\s0  This is the default for processors that are known to
  support these registers.  When using the o32 \s-1FPXX ABI,\s0 **-mno-odd-spreg**
  is set by default.
* **-mabs=2008**  
  .IX Item "-mabs=2008"
* **-mabs=legacy**  
  .IX Item "-mabs=legacy"
  These options control the treatment of the special not-a-number (NaN)
  \s-1IEEE 754\s0 floating-point data with the \f(CW`abs.\f(CIfmt\f(CW\*(C' and
  \f(CW`neg.\f(CIfmt\f(CW\*(C' machine instructions.
  .Sp
  By default or when **-mabs=legacy** is used the legacy
  treatment is selected.  In this case these instructions are considered
  arithmetic and avoided where correct operation is required and the
  input operand might be a NaN.  A longer sequence of instructions that
  manipulate the sign bit of floating-point datum manually is used
  instead unless the **-ffinite-math-only** option has also been
  specified.
  .Sp
  The **-mabs=2008** option selects the \s-1IEEE 754-2008\s0 treatment.  In
  this case these instructions are considered non-arithmetic and therefore
  operating correctly in all cases, including in particular where the
  input operand is a NaN.  These instructions are therefore always used
  for the respective operations.
* **-mnan=2008**  
  .IX Item "-mnan=2008"
* **-mnan=legacy**  
  .IX Item "-mnan=legacy"
  These options control the encoding of the special not-a-number (NaN)
  \s-1IEEE 754\s0 floating-point data.
  .Sp
  The **-mnan=legacy** option selects the legacy encoding.  In this
  case quiet NaNs (qNaNs) are denoted by the first bit of their trailing
  significand field being 0, whereas signaling NaNs (sNaNs) are denoted
  by the first bit of their trailing significand field being 1.
  .Sp
  The **-mnan=2008** option selects the \s-1IEEE 754-2008\s0 encoding.  In
  this case qNaNs are denoted by the first bit of their trailing
  significand field being 1, whereas sNaNs are denoted by the first bit of
  their trailing significand field being 0.
  .Sp
  The default is **-mnan=legacy** unless \s-1GCC\s0 has been configured with
  **--with-nan=2008**.
* **-mllsc**  
  .IX Item "-mllsc"
* **-mno-llsc**  
  .IX Item "-mno-llsc"
  Use (do not use) **ll**, **sc**, and **sync** instructions to
  implement atomic memory built-in functions.  When neither option is
  specified, \s-1GCC\s0 uses the instructions if the target architecture
  supports them.
  .Sp
  **-mllsc** is useful if the runtime environment can emulate the
  instructions and **-mno-llsc** can be useful when compiling for
  nonstandard ISAs.  You can make either option the default by
  configuring \s-1GCC\s0 with **--with-llsc** and **--without-llsc**
  respectively.  **--with-llsc** is the default for some
  configurations; see the installation documentation for details.
* **-mdsp**  
  .IX Item "-mdsp"
* **-mno-dsp**  
  .IX Item "-mno-dsp"
  Use (do not use) revision 1 of the \s-1MIPS DSP ASE.\s0
    This option defines the
  preprocessor macro \f(CW`\_\|\_mips\_dsp\*(C'.  It also defines
  \f(CW`\_\|\_mips\_dsp\_rev\*(C' to 1.
* **-mdspr2**  
  .IX Item "-mdspr2"
* **-mno-dspr2**  
  .IX Item "-mno-dspr2"
  Use (do not use) revision 2 of the \s-1MIPS DSP ASE.\s0
    This option defines the
  preprocessor macros \f(CW`\_\|\_mips\_dsp\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`\_\|\_mips\_dspr2\*(C'.
  It also defines \f(CW`\_\|\_mips\_dsp\_rev\*(C' to 2.
* **-msmartmips**  
  .IX Item "-msmartmips"
* **-mno-smartmips**  
  .IX Item "-mno-smartmips"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 SmartMIPS \s-1ASE.\s0
* **-mpaired-single**  
  .IX Item "-mpaired-single"
* **-mno-paired-single**  
  .IX Item "-mno-paired-single"
  Use (do not use) paired-single floating-point instructions.
    This option requires
  hardware floating-point support to be enabled.
* **-mdmx**  
  .IX Item "-mdmx"
* **-mno-mdmx**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mdmx"
  Use (do not use) \s-1MIPS\s0 Digital Media Extension instructions.
  This option can only be used when generating 64-bit code and requires
  hardware floating-point support to be enabled.
* **-mips3d**  
  .IX Item "-mips3d"
* **-mno-mips3d**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mips3d"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS-3D ASE.\s0  
  The option **-mips3d** implies **-mpaired-single**.
* **-mmicromips**  
  .IX Item "-mmicromips"
* **-mno-micromips**  
  .IX Item "-mno-micromips"
  Generate (do not generate) microMIPS code.
  .Sp
  MicroMIPS code generation can also be controlled on a per-function basis
  by means of \f(CW`micromips\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`nomicromips\*(C' attributes.
* **-mmt**  
  .IX Item "-mmt"
* **-mno-mt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mt"
  Use (do not use) \s-1MT\s0 Multithreading instructions.
* **-mmcu**  
  .IX Item "-mmcu"
* **-mno-mcu**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mcu"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS MCU ASE\s0 instructions.
* **-meva**  
  .IX Item "-meva"
* **-mno-eva**  
  .IX Item "-mno-eva"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Enhanced Virtual Addressing instructions.
* **-mvirt**  
  .IX Item "-mvirt"
* **-mno-virt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-virt"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Virtualization (\s-1VZ\s0) instructions.
* **-mxpa**  
  .IX Item "-mxpa"
* **-mno-xpa**  
  .IX Item "-mno-xpa"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 eXtended Physical Address (\s-1XPA\s0) instructions.
* **-mcrc**  
  .IX Item "-mcrc"
* **-mno-crc**  
  .IX Item "-mno-crc"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Cyclic Redundancy Check (\s-1CRC\s0) instructions.
* **-mginv**  
  .IX Item "-mginv"
* **-mno-ginv**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ginv"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Global INValidate (\s-1GINV\s0) instructions.
* **-mloongson-mmi**  
  .IX Item "-mloongson-mmi"
* **-mno-loongson-mmi**  
  .IX Item "-mno-loongson-mmi"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Loongson MultiMedia extensions Instructions (\s-1MMI\s0).
* **-mloongson-ext**  
  .IX Item "-mloongson-ext"
* **-mno-loongson-ext**  
  .IX Item "-mno-loongson-ext"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Loongson EXTensions (\s-1EXT\s0) instructions.
* **-mloongson-ext2**  
  .IX Item "-mloongson-ext2"
* **-mno-loongson-ext2**  
  .IX Item "-mno-loongson-ext2"
  Use (do not use) the \s-1MIPS\s0 Loongson EXTensions r2 (\s-1EXT2\s0) instructions.
* **-mlong64**  
  .IX Item "-mlong64"
  Force \f(CW`long\*(C' types to be 64 bits wide.  See **-mlong32** for
  an explanation of the default and the way that the pointer size is
  determined.
* **-mlong32**  
  .IX Item "-mlong32"
  Force \f(CW`long\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`int\*(C', and pointer types to be 32 bits wide.
  .Sp
  The default size of \f(CW`int\*(C's, \f(CW\*(C\`long\*(C's and pointers depends on
  the \s-1ABI.\s0  All the supported ABIs use 32-bit \f(CW`int\*(C's.  The n64 \s-1ABI\s0
  uses 64-bit \f(CW`long\*(C's, as does the 64-bit \s-1EABI\s0; the others use
  32-bit \f(CW`long\*(C's.  Pointers are the same size as \f(CW\*(C\`long\*(C's,
  or the same size as integer registers, whichever is smaller.
* **-msym32**  
  .IX Item "-msym32"
* **-mno-sym32**  
  .IX Item "-mno-sym32"
  Assume (do not assume) that all symbols have 32-bit values, regardless
  of the selected \s-1ABI.\s0  This option is useful in combination with
  **-mabi=64** and **-mno-abicalls** because it allows \s-1GCC\s0
  to generate shorter and faster references to symbolic addresses.
* **-G** _num_  
  .IX Item "-G num"
  Put definitions of externally-visible data in a small data section
  if that data is no bigger than _num_ bytes.  \s-1GCC\s0 can then generate
  more efficient accesses to the data; see **-mgpopt** for details.
  .Sp
  The default **-G** option depends on the configuration.
* **-mlocal-sdata**  
  .IX Item "-mlocal-sdata"
* **-mno-local-sdata**  
  .IX Item "-mno-local-sdata"
  Extend (do not extend) the **-G** behavior to local data too,
  such as to static variables in C.  **-mlocal-sdata** is the
  default for all configurations.
  .Sp
  If the linker complains that an application is using too much small data,
  you might want to try rebuilding the less performance-critical parts with
  **-mno-local-sdata**.  You might also want to build large
  libraries with **-mno-local-sdata**, so that the libraries leave
  more room for the main program.
* **-mextern-sdata**  
  .IX Item "-mextern-sdata"
* **-mno-extern-sdata**  
  .IX Item "-mno-extern-sdata"
  Assume (do not assume) that externally-defined data is in
  a small data section if the size of that data is within the **-G** limit.
  **-mextern-sdata** is the default for all configurations.
  .Sp
  If you compile a module _Mod_ with **-mextern-sdata** **-G**
  _num_ **-mgpopt**, and _Mod_ references a variable _Var_
  that is no bigger than _num_ bytes, you must make sure that _Var_
  is placed in a small data section.  If _Var_ is defined by another
  module, you must either compile that module with a high-enough
  **-G** setting or attach a \f(CW`section\*(C' attribute to _Var_'s
  definition.  If _Var_ is common, you must link the application
  with a high-enough **-G** setting.
  .Sp
  The easiest way of satisfying these restrictions is to compile
  and link every module with the same **-G** option.  However,
  you may wish to build a library that supports several different
  small data limits.  You can do this by compiling the library with
  the highest supported **-G** setting and additionally using
  **-mno-extern-sdata** to stop the library from making assumptions
  about externally-defined data.
* **-mgpopt**  
  .IX Item "-mgpopt"
* **-mno-gpopt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-gpopt"
  Use (do not use) GP-relative accesses for symbols that are known to be
  in a small data section; see **-G**, **-mlocal-sdata** and
  **-mextern-sdata**.  **-mgpopt** is the default for all
  configurations.
  .Sp
  **-mno-gpopt** is useful for cases where the \f(CW$gp register
  might not hold the value of \f(CW`\_gp\*(C'.  For example, if the code is
  part of a library that might be used in a boot monitor, programs that
  call boot monitor routines pass an unknown value in \f(CW$gp.
  (In such situations, the boot monitor itself is usually compiled
  with **-G0**.)
  .Sp
  **-mno-gpopt** implies **-mno-local-sdata** and
  **-mno-extern-sdata**.
* **-membedded-data**  
  .IX Item "-membedded-data"
* **-mno-embedded-data**  
  .IX Item "-mno-embedded-data"
  Allocate variables to the read-only data section first if possible, then
  next in the small data section if possible, otherwise in data.  This gives
  slightly slower code than the default, but reduces the amount of \s-1RAM\s0 required
  when executing, and thus may be preferred for some embedded systems.
* **-muninit-const-in-rodata**  
  .IX Item "-muninit-const-in-rodata"
* **-mno-uninit-const-in-rodata**  
  .IX Item "-mno-uninit-const-in-rodata"
  Put uninitialized \f(CW`const\*(C' variables in the read-only data section.
  This option is only meaningful in conjunction with **-membedded-data**.
* **-mcode-readable=**_setting_  
  .IX Item "-mcode-readable=setting"
  Specify whether \s-1GCC\s0 may generate code that reads from executable sections.
  There are three possible settings:
    * **-mcode-readable=yes**  
      .IX Item "-mcode-readable=yes"
      Instructions may freely access executable sections.  This is the
      default setting.
    * **-mcode-readable=pcrel**  
      .IX Item "-mcode-readable=pcrel"
      \s-1MIPS16\s0 PC-relative load instructions can access executable sections,
      but other instructions must not do so.  This option is useful on 4KSc
      and 4KSd processors when the code TLBs have the Read Inhibit bit set.
      It is also useful on processors that can be configured to have a dual
      instruction/data \s-1SRAM\s0 interface and that, like the M4K, automatically
      redirect PC-relative loads to the instruction \s-1RAM.\s0
    * **-mcode-readable=no**  
      .IX Item "-mcode-readable=no"
      Instructions must not access executable sections.  This option can be
      useful on targets that are configured to have a dual instruction/data
      \s-1SRAM\s0 interface but that (unlike the M4K) do not automatically redirect
      PC-relative loads to the instruction \s-1RAM.\s0
* **-msplit-addresses**  
  .IX Item "-msplit-addresses"
* **-mno-split-addresses**  
  .IX Item "-mno-split-addresses"
  Enable (disable) use of the \f(CW`%hi()\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`%lo()\*(C' assembler
  relocation operators.  This option has been superseded by
  **-mexplicit-relocs** but is retained for backwards compatibility.
* **-mexplicit-relocs**  
  .IX Item "-mexplicit-relocs"
* **-mno-explicit-relocs**  
  .IX Item "-mno-explicit-relocs"
  Use (do not use) assembler relocation operators when dealing with symbolic
  addresses.  The alternative, selected by **-mno-explicit-relocs**,
  is to use assembler macros instead.
  .Sp
  **-mexplicit-relocs** is the default if \s-1GCC\s0 was configured
  to use an assembler that supports relocation operators.
* **-mcheck-zero-division**  
  .IX Item "-mcheck-zero-division"
* **-mno-check-zero-division**  
  .IX Item "-mno-check-zero-division"
  Trap (do not trap) on integer division by zero.
  .Sp
  The default is **-mcheck-zero-division**.
* **-mdivide-traps**  
  .IX Item "-mdivide-traps"
* **-mdivide-breaks**  
  .IX Item "-mdivide-breaks"
  \s-1MIPS\s0 systems check for division by zero by generating either a
  conditional trap or a break instruction.  Using traps results in
  smaller code, but is only supported on \s-1MIPS II\s0 and later.  Also, some
  versions of the Linux kernel have a bug that prevents trap from
  generating the proper signal (\f(CW`SIGFPE\*(C').  Use **-mdivide-traps** to
  allow conditional traps on architectures that support them and
  **-mdivide-breaks** to force the use of breaks.
  .Sp
  The default is usually **-mdivide-traps**, but this can be
  overridden at configure time using **--with-divide=breaks**.
  Divide-by-zero checks can be completely disabled using
  **-mno-check-zero-division**.
* **-mload-store-pairs**  
  .IX Item "-mload-store-pairs"
* **-mno-load-store-pairs**  
  .IX Item "-mno-load-store-pairs"
  Enable (disable) an optimization that pairs consecutive load or store
  instructions to enable load/store bonding.  This option is enabled by
  default but only takes effect when the selected architecture is known
  to support bonding.
* **-mmemcpy**  
  .IX Item "-mmemcpy"
* **-mno-memcpy**  
  .IX Item "-mno-memcpy"
  Force (do not force) the use of \f(CW`memcpy\*(C' for non-trivial block
  moves.  The default is **-mno-memcpy**, which allows \s-1GCC\s0 to inline
  most constant-sized copies.
* **-mlong-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mlong-calls"
* **-mno-long-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mno-long-calls"
  Disable (do not disable) use of the \f(CW`jal\*(C' instruction.  Calling
  functions using \f(CW`jal\*(C' is more efficient but requires the caller
  and callee to be in the same 256 megabyte segment.
  .Sp
  This option has no effect on abicalls code.  The default is
  **-mno-long-calls**.
* **-mmad**  
  .IX Item "-mmad"
* **-mno-mad**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mad"
  Enable (disable) use of the \f(CW`mad\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`madu\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`mul\*(C'
  instructions, as provided by the R4650 \s-1ISA.\s0
* **-mimadd**  
  .IX Item "-mimadd"
* **-mno-imadd**  
  .IX Item "-mno-imadd"
  Enable (disable) use of the \f(CW`madd\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`msub\*(C' integer
  instructions.  The default is **-mimadd** on architectures
  that support \f(CW`madd\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`msub\*(C' except for the 74k 
  architecture where it was found to generate slower code.
* **-mfused-madd**  
  .IX Item "-mfused-madd"
* **-mno-fused-madd**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fused-madd"
  Enable (disable) use of the floating-point multiply-accumulate
  instructions, when they are available.  The default is
  **-mfused-madd**.
  .Sp
  On the R8000 \s-1CPU\s0 when multiply-accumulate instructions are used,
  the intermediate product is calculated to infinite precision
  and is not subject to the \s-1FCSR\s0 Flush to Zero bit.  This may be
  undesirable in some circumstances.  On other processors the result
  is numerically identical to the equivalent computation using
  separate multiply, add, subtract and negate instructions.
* **-nocpp**  
  .IX Item "-nocpp"
  Tell the \s-1MIPS\s0 assembler to not run its preprocessor over user
  assembler files (with a **.s** suffix) when assembling them.
* **-mfix-24k**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-24k"
* **-mno-fix-24k**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-24k"
  Work around the 24K E48 (lost data on stores during refill) errata.
  The workarounds are implemented by the assembler rather than by \s-1GCC.\s0
* **-mfix-r4000**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-r4000"
* **-mno-fix-r4000**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-r4000"
  Work around certain R4000 \s-1CPU\s0 errata:
    * A double-word or a variable shift may give an incorrect result if executed
      immediately after starting an integer division.
    * A double-word or a variable shift may give an incorrect result if executed
      while an integer multiplication is in progress.
    * An integer division may give an incorrect result if started in a delay slot
      of a taken branch or a jump.
* **-mfix-r4400**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-r4400"
* **-mno-fix-r4400**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-r4400"
  Work around certain R4400 \s-1CPU\s0 errata:
    * A double-word or a variable shift may give an incorrect result if executed
      immediately after starting an integer division.
* **-mfix-r10000**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-r10000"
* **-mno-fix-r10000**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-r10000"
  Work around certain R10000 errata:
    * \f(CW`ll\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`sc\*(C' sequences may not behave atomically on revisions
      prior to 3.0.  They may deadlock on revisions 2.6 and earlier.
      .Sp
      This option can only be used if the target architecture supports
      branch-likely instructions.  **-mfix-r10000** is the default when
      **-march=r10000** is used; **-mno-fix-r10000** is the default
      otherwise.
* **-mfix-r5900**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-r5900"
* **-mno-fix-r5900**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-r5900"
  Do not attempt to schedule the preceding instruction into the delay slot
  of a branch instruction placed at the end of a short loop of six
  instructions or fewer and always schedule a \f(CW`nop\*(C' instruction there
  instead.  The short loop bug under certain conditions causes loops to
  execute only once or twice, due to a hardware bug in the R5900 chip.  The
  workaround is implemented by the assembler rather than by \s-1GCC.\s0
* **-mfix-rm7000**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-rm7000"
* **-mno-fix-rm7000**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-rm7000"
  Work around the \s-1RM7000\s0 \f(CW`dmult\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`dmultu\*(C' errata.  The
  workarounds are implemented by the assembler rather than by \s-1GCC.\s0
* **-mfix-vr4120**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-vr4120"
* **-mno-fix-vr4120**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-vr4120"
  Work around certain \s-1VR4120\s0 errata:
    * \f(CW`dmultu\*(C' does not always produce the correct result.
    * \f(CW`div\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`ddiv\*(C' do not always produce the correct result if one
      of the operands is negative.
      .Sp
      The workarounds for the division errata rely on special functions in
      _libgcc.a_.  At present, these functions are only provided by
      the \f(CW`mips64vr*-elf\*(C' configurations.
      .Sp
      Other \s-1VR4120\s0 errata require a \s-1NOP\s0 to be inserted between certain pairs of
      instructions.  These errata are handled by the assembler, not by \s-1GCC\s0 itself.
* **-mfix-vr4130**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-vr4130"
  Work around the \s-1VR4130\s0 \f(CW`mflo\*(C'/\f(CW\*(C\`mfhi\*(C' errata.  The
  workarounds are implemented by the assembler rather than by \s-1GCC,\s0
  although \s-1GCC\s0 avoids using \f(CW`mflo\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`mfhi\*(C' if the
  \s-1VR4130\s0 \f(CW`macc\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`macchi\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`dmacc\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`dmacchi\*(C'
  instructions are available instead.
* **-mfix-sb1**  
  .IX Item "-mfix-sb1"
* **-mno-fix-sb1**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fix-sb1"
  Work around certain \s-1SB-1 CPU\s0 core errata.
  (This flag currently works around the \s-1SB-1\s0 revision 2
  F1\*(R" and \*(L"F2\*(R" floating-point errata.)
* **-mr10k-cache-barrier=**_setting_  
  .IX Item "-mr10k-cache-barrier=setting"
  Specify whether \s-1GCC\s0 should insert cache barriers to avoid the
  side effects of speculation on R10K processors.
  .Sp
  In common with many processors, the R10K tries to predict the outcome
  of a conditional branch and speculatively executes instructions from
  the taken\*(R" branch.  It later aborts these instructions if the
  predicted outcome is wrong.  However, on the R10K, even aborted
  instructions can have side effects.
  .Sp
  This problem only affects kernel stores and, depending on the system,
  kernel loads.  As an example, a speculatively-executed store may load
  the target memory into cache and mark the cache line as dirty, even if
  the store itself is later aborted.  If a \s-1DMA\s0 operation writes to the
  same area of memory before the dirty\*(R" line is flushed, the cached
  data overwrites the DMA-ed data.  See the R10K processor manual
  for a full description, including other potential problems.
  .Sp
  One workaround is to insert cache barrier instructions before every memory
  access that might be speculatively executed and that might have side
  effects even if aborted.  **-mr10k-cache-barrier=**_setting_
  controls \s-1GCC\s0's implementation of this workaround.  It assumes that
  aborted accesses to any byte in the following regions does not have
  side effects:
    * 1.  
      .IX Item "1."
      the memory occupied by the current function's stack frame;
    * 2.  
      .IX Item "2."
      the memory occupied by an incoming stack argument;
    * 3.  
      .IX Item "3."
      the memory occupied by an object with a link-time-constant address.
      .Sp
      It is the kernel's responsibility to ensure that speculative
      accesses to these regions are indeed safe.
      .Sp
      If the input program contains a function declaration such as:
      .Sp
      .Vb 1
              void foo (void);
      .Ve
      .Sp
      then the implementation of \f(CW`foo\*(C' must allow \f(CW\*(C\`j foo\*(C' and
      \f(CW`jal foo\*(C' to be executed speculatively.  \s-1GCC\s0 honors this
      restriction for functions it compiles itself.  It expects non-GCC
      functions (such as hand-written assembly code) to do the same.
      .Sp
      The option has three forms:
    * **-mr10k-cache-barrier=load-store**  
      .IX Item "-mr10k-cache-barrier=load-store"
      Insert a cache barrier before a load or store that might be
      speculatively executed and that might have side effects even
      if aborted.
    * **-mr10k-cache-barrier=store**  
      .IX Item "-mr10k-cache-barrier=store"
      Insert a cache barrier before a store that might be speculatively
      executed and that might have side effects even if aborted.
    * **-mr10k-cache-barrier=none**  
      .IX Item "-mr10k-cache-barrier=none"
      Disable the insertion of cache barriers.  This is the default setting.
* **-mflush-func=**_func_  
  .IX Item "-mflush-func=func"
* **-mno-flush-func**  
  .IX Item "-mno-flush-func"
  Specifies the function to call to flush the I and D caches, or to not
  call any such function.  If called, the function must take the same
  arguments as the common \f(CW`\_flush\_func\*(C', that is, the address of the
  memory range for which the cache is being flushed, the size of the
  memory range, and the number 3 (to flush both caches).  The default
  depends on the target \s-1GCC\s0 was configured for, but commonly is either
  \f(CW`\_flush\_func\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`\_\|\_cpu\_flush\*(C'.
* **mbranch-cost=**_num_  
  .IX Item "mbranch-cost=num"
  Set the cost of branches to roughly _num_ simple\*(R" instructions.
  This cost is only a heuristic and is not guaranteed to produce
  consistent results across releases.  A zero cost redundantly selects
  the default, which is based on the **-mtune** setting.
* **-mbranch-likely**  
  .IX Item "-mbranch-likely"
* **-mno-branch-likely**  
  .IX Item "-mno-branch-likely"
  Enable or disable use of Branch Likely instructions, regardless of the
  default for the selected architecture.  By default, Branch Likely
  instructions may be generated if they are supported by the selected
  architecture.  An exception is for the \s-1MIPS32\s0 and \s-1MIPS64\s0 architectures
  and processors that implement those architectures; for those, Branch
  Likely instructions are not be generated by default because the \s-1MIPS32\s0
  and \s-1MIPS64\s0 architectures specifically deprecate their use.
* **-mcompact-branches=never**  
  .IX Item "-mcompact-branches=never"
* **-mcompact-branches=optimal**  
  .IX Item "-mcompact-branches=optimal"
* **-mcompact-branches=always**  
  .IX Item "-mcompact-branches=always"
  These options control which form of branches will be generated.  The
  default is **-mcompact-branches=optimal**.
  .Sp
  The **-mcompact-branches=never** option ensures that compact branch
  instructions will never be generated.
  .Sp
  The **-mcompact-branches=always** option ensures that a compact
  branch instruction will be generated if available.  If a compact branch
  instruction is not available, a delay slot form of the branch will be
  used instead.
  .Sp
  This option is supported from \s-1MIPS\s0 Release 6 onwards.
  .Sp
  The **-mcompact-branches=optimal** option will cause a delay slot
  branch to be used if one is available in the current \s-1ISA\s0 and the delay
  slot is successfully filled.  If the delay slot is not filled, a compact
  branch will be chosen if one is available.
* **-mfp-exceptions**  
  .IX Item "-mfp-exceptions"
* **-mno-fp-exceptions**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fp-exceptions"
  Specifies whether \s-1FP\s0 exceptions are enabled.  This affects how
  \s-1FP\s0 instructions are scheduled for some processors.
  The default is that \s-1FP\s0 exceptions are
  enabled.
  .Sp
  For instance, on the \s-1SB-1,\s0 if \s-1FP\s0 exceptions are disabled, and we are emitting
  64-bit code, then we can use both \s-1FP\s0 pipes.  Otherwise, we can only use one
  \s-1FP\s0 pipe.
* **-mvr4130-align**  
  .IX Item "-mvr4130-align"
* **-mno-vr4130-align**  
  .IX Item "-mno-vr4130-align"
  The \s-1VR4130\s0 pipeline is two-way superscalar, but can only issue two
  instructions together if the first one is 8-byte aligned.  When this
  option is enabled, \s-1GCC\s0 aligns pairs of instructions that it
  thinks should execute in parallel.
  .Sp
  This option only has an effect when optimizing for the \s-1VR4130.\s0
  It normally makes code faster, but at the expense of making it bigger.
  It is enabled by default at optimization level **-O3**.
* **-msynci**  
  .IX Item "-msynci"
* **-mno-synci**  
  .IX Item "-mno-synci"
  Enable (disable) generation of \f(CW`synci\*(C' instructions on
  architectures that support it.  The \f(CW`synci\*(C' instructions (if
  enabled) are generated when \f(CW`\_\|\_builtin\_\|\_\|\_clear\_cache\*(C' is
  compiled.
  .Sp
  This option defaults to **-mno-synci**, but the default can be
  overridden by configuring \s-1GCC\s0 with **--with-synci**.
  .Sp
  When compiling code for single processor systems, it is generally safe
  to use \f(CW`synci\*(C'.  However, on many multi-core (\s-1SMP\s0) systems, it
  does not invalidate the instruction caches on all cores and may lead
  to undefined behavior.
* **-mrelax-pic-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mrelax-pic-calls"
* **-mno-relax-pic-calls**  
  .IX Item "-mno-relax-pic-calls"
  Try to turn \s-1PIC\s0 calls that are normally dispatched via register
  \f(CW$25 into direct calls.  This is only possible if the linker can
  resolve the destination at link time and if the destination is within
  range for a direct call.
  .Sp
  **-mrelax-pic-calls** is the default if \s-1GCC\s0 was configured to use
  an assembler and a linker that support the \f(CW`.reloc\*(C' assembly
  directive and **-mexplicit-relocs** is in effect.  With
  **-mno-explicit-relocs**, this optimization can be performed by the
  assembler and the linker alone without help from the compiler.
* **-mmcount-ra-address**  
  .IX Item "-mmcount-ra-address"
* **-mno-mcount-ra-address**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mcount-ra-address"
  Emit (do not emit) code that allows \f(CW`\_mcount\*(C' to modify the
  calling function's return address.  When enabled, this option extends
  the usual \f(CW`\_mcount\*(C' interface with a new _ra-address_
  parameter, which has type \f(CW`intptr_t *\*(C' and is passed in register
  \f(CW$12.  \f(CW`\_mcount\*(C' can then modify the return address by
  doing both of the following:
    * *  
      Returning the new address in register \f(CW$31.
    * *  
      Storing the new address in \f(CW`*\f(CIra-address\f(CW\*(C',
      if _ra-address_ is nonnull.
      .Sp
      The default is **-mno-mcount-ra-address**.
* **-mframe-header-opt**  
  .IX Item "-mframe-header-opt"
* **-mno-frame-header-opt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-frame-header-opt"
  Enable (disable) frame header optimization in the o32 \s-1ABI.\s0  When using the
  o32 \s-1ABI,\s0 calling functions will allocate 16 bytes on the stack for the called
  function to write out register arguments.  When enabled, this optimization
  will suppress the allocation of the frame header if it can be determined that
  it is unused.
  .Sp
  This optimization is off by default at all optimization levels.
* **-mlxc1-sxc1**  
  .IX Item "-mlxc1-sxc1"
* **-mno-lxc1-sxc1**  
  .IX Item "-mno-lxc1-sxc1"
  When applicable, enable (disable) the generation of \f(CW`lwxc1\*(C',
  \f(CW`swxc1\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`ldxc1\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`sdxc1\*(C' instructions.  Enabled by default.
* **-mmadd4**  
  .IX Item "-mmadd4"
* **-mno-madd4**  
  .IX Item "-mno-madd4"
  When applicable, enable (disable) the generation of 4-operand \f(CW`madd.s\*(C',
  \f(CW`madd.d\*(C' and related instructions.  Enabled by default.

<a name="s-1mmixs0-options"></a>

### \s-1MMIX\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "MMIX Options"
These options are defined for the \s-1MMIX:\s0

* **-mlibfuncs**  
  .IX Item "-mlibfuncs"
* **-mno-libfuncs**  
  .IX Item "-mno-libfuncs"
  Specify that intrinsic library functions are being compiled, passing all
  values in registers, no matter the size.
* **-mepsilon**  
  .IX Item "-mepsilon"
* **-mno-epsilon**  
  .IX Item "-mno-epsilon"
  Generate floating-point comparison instructions that compare with respect
  to the \f(CW`rE\*(C' epsilon register.
* **-mabi=mmixware**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=mmixware"
* **-mabi=gnu**  
  .IX Item "-mabi=gnu"
  Generate code that passes function parameters and return values that (in
  the called function) are seen as registers \f(CW$0 and up, as opposed to
  the \s-1GNU ABI\s0 which uses global registers \f(CW$231 and up.
* **-mzero-extend**  
  .IX Item "-mzero-extend"
* **-mno-zero-extend**  
  .IX Item "-mno-zero-extend"
  When reading data from memory in sizes shorter than 64 bits, use (do not
  use) zero-extending load instructions by default, rather than
  sign-extending ones.
* **-mknuthdiv**  
  .IX Item "-mknuthdiv"
* **-mno-knuthdiv**  
  .IX Item "-mno-knuthdiv"
  Make the result of a division yielding a remainder have the same sign as
  the divisor.  With the default, **-mno-knuthdiv**, the sign of the
  remainder follows the sign of the dividend.  Both methods are
  arithmetically valid, the latter being almost exclusively used.
* **-mtoplevel-symbols**  
  .IX Item "-mtoplevel-symbols"
* **-mno-toplevel-symbols**  
  .IX Item "-mno-toplevel-symbols"
  Prepend (do not prepend) a **:** to all global symbols, so the assembly
  code can be used with the \f(CW`PREFIX\*(C' assembly directive.
* **-melf**  
  .IX Item "-melf"
  Generate an executable in the \s-1ELF\s0 format, rather than the default
  **mmo** format used by the **mmix** simulator.
* **-mbranch-predict**  
  .IX Item "-mbranch-predict"
* **-mno-branch-predict**  
  .IX Item "-mno-branch-predict"
  Use (do not use) the probable-branch instructions, when static branch
  prediction indicates a probable branch.
* **-mbase-addresses**  
  .IX Item "-mbase-addresses"
* **-mno-base-addresses**  
  .IX Item "-mno-base-addresses"
  Generate (do not generate) code that uses _base addresses_.  Using a
  base address automatically generates a request (handled by the assembler
  and the linker) for a constant to be set up in a global register.  The
  register is used for one or more base address requests within the range 0
  to 255 from the value held in the register.  The generally leads to short
  and fast code, but the number of different data items that can be
  addressed is limited.  This means that a program that uses lots of static
  data may require **-mno-base-addresses**.
* **-msingle-exit**  
  .IX Item "-msingle-exit"
* **-mno-single-exit**  
  .IX Item "-mno-single-exit"
  Force (do not force) generated code to have a single exit point in each
  function.

<a name="s-1mn10300s0-options"></a>

### \s-1MN10300\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "MN10300 Options"
These **-m** options are defined for Matsushita \s-1MN10300\s0 architectures:

* **-mmult-bug**  
  .IX Item "-mmult-bug"
  Generate code to avoid bugs in the multiply instructions for the \s-1MN10300\s0
  processors.  This is the default.
* **-mno-mult-bug**  
  .IX Item "-mno-mult-bug"
  Do not generate code to avoid bugs in the multiply instructions for the
  \s-1MN10300\s0 processors.
* **-mam33**  
  .IX Item "-mam33"
  Generate code using features specific to the \s-1AM33\s0 processor.
* **-mno-am33**  
  .IX Item "-mno-am33"
  Do not generate code using features specific to the \s-1AM33\s0 processor.  This
  is the default.
* **-mam33-2**  
  .IX Item "-mam33-2"
  Generate code using features specific to the \s-1AM33/2.0\s0 processor.
* **-mam34**  
  .IX Item "-mam34"
  Generate code using features specific to the \s-1AM34\s0 processor.
* **-mtune=**_cpu-type_  
  .IX Item "-mtune=cpu-type"
  Use the timing characteristics of the indicated \s-1CPU\s0 type when
  scheduling instructions.  This does not change the targeted processor
  type.  The \s-1CPU\s0 type must be one of **mn10300**, **am33**,
  **am33-2** or **am34**.
* **-mreturn-pointer-on-d0**  
  .IX Item "-mreturn-pointer-on-d0"
  When generating a function that returns a pointer, return the pointer
  in both \f(CW`a0\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`d0\*(C'.  Otherwise, the pointer is returned
  only in \f(CW`a0\*(C', and attempts to call such functions without a prototype
  result in errors.  Note that this option is on by default; use
  **-mno-return-pointer-on-d0** to disable it.
* **-mno-crt0**  
  .IX Item "-mno-crt0"
  Do not link in the C run-time initialization object file.
* **-mrelax**  
  .IX Item "-mrelax"
  Indicate to the linker that it should perform a relaxation optimization pass
  to shorten branches, calls and absolute memory addresses.  This option only
  has an effect when used on the command line for the final link step.
  .Sp
  This option makes symbolic debugging impossible.
* **-mliw**  
  .IX Item "-mliw"
  Allow the compiler to generate _Long Instruction Word_
  instructions if the target is the **\s-1AM33\s0** or later.  This is the
  default.  This option defines the preprocessor macro \f(CW`\_\|\_LIW\_\|\_\*(C'.
* **-mno-liw**  
  .IX Item "-mno-liw"
  Do not allow the compiler to generate _Long Instruction Word_
  instructions.  This option defines the preprocessor macro
  \f(CW`\_\|\_NO\_LIW\_\|\_\*(C'.
* **-msetlb**  
  .IX Item "-msetlb"
  Allow the compiler to generate the _\s-1SETLB\s0_ and _Lcc_
  instructions if the target is the **\s-1AM33\s0** or later.  This is the
  default.  This option defines the preprocessor macro \f(CW`\_\|\_SETLB\_\|\_\*(C'.
* **-mno-setlb**  
  .IX Item "-mno-setlb"
  Do not allow the compiler to generate _\s-1SETLB\s0_ or _Lcc_
  instructions.  This option defines the preprocessor macro
  \f(CW`\_\|\_NO\_SETLB\_\|\_\*(C'.

<a name="moxie-options"></a>

### Moxie Options

.IX Subsection "Moxie Options"

* **-meb**  
  .IX Item "-meb"
  Generate big-endian code.  This is the default for **moxie-*-***
  configurations.
* **-mel**  
  .IX Item "-mel"
  Generate little-endian code.
* **-mmul.x**  
  .IX Item "-mmul.x"
  Generate mul.x and umul.x instructions.  This is the default for
  **moxiebox-*-*** configurations.
* **-mno-crt0**  
  .IX Item "-mno-crt0"
  Do not link in the C run-time initialization object file.

<a name="s-1msp430s0-options"></a>

### \s-1MSP430\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "MSP430 Options"
These options are defined for the \s-1MSP430:\s0

* **-masm-hex**  
  .IX Item "-masm-hex"
  Force assembly output to always use hex constants.  Normally such
  constants are signed decimals, but this option is available for
  testsuite and/or aesthetic purposes.
* **-mmcu=**  
  .IX Item "-mmcu="
  Select the \s-1MCU\s0 to target.  This is used to create a C preprocessor
  symbol based upon the \s-1MCU\s0 name, converted to upper case and pre- and
  post-fixed with **\_\|\_**.  This in turn is used by the
  _msp430.h_ header file to select an MCU-specific supplementary
  header file.
  .Sp
  The option also sets the \s-1ISA\s0 to use.  If the \s-1MCU\s0 name is one that is
  known to only support the 430 \s-1ISA\s0 then that is selected, otherwise the
  430X \s-1ISA\s0 is selected.  A generic \s-1MCU\s0 name of **msp430** can also be
  used to select the 430 \s-1ISA.\s0  Similarly the generic **msp430x** \s-1MCU\s0
  name selects the 430X \s-1ISA.\s0
  .Sp
  In addition an MCU-specific linker script is added to the linker
  command line.  The script's name is the name of the \s-1MCU\s0 with
  _.ld_ appended.  Thus specifying **-mmcu=xxx** on the **gcc**
  command line defines the C preprocessor symbol \f(CW`\_\|\_XXX\_\|\_\*(C' and
  cause the linker to search for a script called _xxx.ld_.
  .Sp
  This option is also passed on to the assembler.
* **-mwarn-mcu**  
  .IX Item "-mwarn-mcu"
* **-mno-warn-mcu**  
  .IX Item "-mno-warn-mcu"
  This option enables or disables warnings about conflicts between the
  \s-1MCU\s0 name specified by the **-mmcu** option and the \s-1ISA\s0 set by the
  **-mcpu** option and/or the hardware multiply support set by the
  **-mhwmult** option.  It also toggles warnings about unrecognized
  \s-1MCU\s0 names.  This option is on by default.
* **-mcpu=**  
  .IX Item "-mcpu="
  Specifies the \s-1ISA\s0 to use.  Accepted values are **msp430**,
  **msp430x** and **msp430xv2**.  This option is deprecated.  The
  **-mmcu=** option should be used to select the \s-1ISA.\s0
* **-msim**  
  .IX Item "-msim"
  Link to the simulator runtime libraries and linker script.  Overrides
  any scripts that would be selected by the **-mmcu=** option.
* **-mlarge**  
  .IX Item "-mlarge"
  Use large-model addressing (20-bit pointers, 32-bit \f(CW`size\_t\*(C').
* **-msmall**  
  .IX Item "-msmall"
  Use small-model addressing (16-bit pointers, 16-bit \f(CW`size\_t\*(C').
* **-mrelax**  
  .IX Item "-mrelax"
  This option is passed to the assembler and linker, and allows the
  linker to perform certain optimizations that cannot be done until
  the final link.
* **mhwmult=**  
  .IX Item "mhwmult="
  Describes the type of hardware multiply supported by the target.
  Accepted values are **none** for no hardware multiply, **16bit**
  for the original 16-bit-only multiply supported by early MCUs.
  **32bit** for the 16/32-bit multiply supported by later MCUs and
  **f5series** for the 16/32-bit multiply supported by F5-series MCUs.
  A value of **auto** can also be given.  This tells \s-1GCC\s0 to deduce
  the hardware multiply support based upon the \s-1MCU\s0 name provided by the
  **-mmcu** option.  If no **-mmcu** option is specified or if
  the \s-1MCU\s0 name is not recognized then no hardware multiply support is
  assumed.  \f(CW`auto\*(C' is the default setting.
  .Sp
  Hardware multiplies are normally performed by calling a library
  routine.  This saves space in the generated code.  When compiling at
  **-O3** or higher however the hardware multiplier is invoked
  inline.  This makes for bigger, but faster code.
  .Sp
  The hardware multiply routines disable interrupts whilst running and
  restore the previous interrupt state when they finish.  This makes
  them safe to use inside interrupt handlers as well as in normal code.
* **-minrt**  
  .IX Item "-minrt"
  Enable the use of a minimum runtime environment - no static
  initializers or constructors.  This is intended for memory-constrained
  devices.  The compiler includes special symbols in some objects
  that tell the linker and runtime which code fragments are required.
* **-mcode-region=**  
  .IX Item "-mcode-region="
* **-mdata-region=**  
  .IX Item "-mdata-region="
  These options tell the compiler where to place functions and data that
  do not have one of the \f(CW`lower\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`upper\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`either\*(C' or
  \f(CW`section\*(C' attributes.  Possible values are \f(CW\*(C\`lower\*(C',
  \f(CW`upper\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`either\*(C' or \f(CW\*(C\`any\*(C'.  The first three behave
  like the corresponding attribute.  The fourth possible value -
  \f(CW`any\*(C' - is the default.  It leaves placement entirely up to the
  linker script and how it assigns the standard sections
  (\f(CW`.text\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`.data\*(C', etc) to the memory regions.
* **-msilicon-errata=**  
  .IX Item "-msilicon-errata="
  This option passes on a request to assembler to enable the fixes for
  the named silicon errata.
* **-msilicon-errata-warn=**  
  .IX Item "-msilicon-errata-warn="
  This option passes on a request to the assembler to enable warning
  messages when a silicon errata might need to be applied.

<a name="s-1nds32s0-options"></a>

### \s-1NDS32\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "NDS32 Options"
These options are defined for \s-1NDS32\s0 implementations:

* **-mbig-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mbig-endian"
  Generate code in big-endian mode.
* **-mlittle-endian**  
  .IX Item "-mlittle-endian"
  Generate code in little-endian mode.
* **-mreduced-regs**  
  .IX Item "-mreduced-regs"
  Use reduced-set registers for register allocation.
* **-mfull-regs**  
  .IX Item "-mfull-regs"
  Use full-set registers for register allocation.
* **-mcmov**  
  .IX Item "-mcmov"
  Generate conditional move instructions.
* **-mno-cmov**  
  .IX Item "-mno-cmov"
  Do not generate conditional move instructions.
* **-mext-perf**  
  .IX Item "-mext-perf"
  Generate performance extension instructions.
* **-mno-ext-perf**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ext-perf"
  Do not generate performance extension instructions.
* **-mext-perf2**  
  .IX Item "-mext-perf2"
  Generate performance extension 2 instructions.
* **-mno-ext-perf2**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ext-perf2"
  Do not generate performance extension 2 instructions.
* **-mext-string**  
  .IX Item "-mext-string"
  Generate string extension instructions.
* **-mno-ext-string**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ext-string"
  Do not generate string extension instructions.
* **-mv3push**  
  .IX Item "-mv3push"
  Generate v3 push25/pop25 instructions.
* **-mno-v3push**  
  .IX Item "-mno-v3push"
  Do not generate v3 push25/pop25 instructions.
* **-m16-bit**  
  .IX Item "-m16-bit"
  Generate 16-bit instructions.
* **-mno-16-bit**  
  .IX Item "-mno-16-bit"
  Do not generate 16-bit instructions.
* **-misr-vector-size=**_num_  
  .IX Item "-misr-vector-size=num"
  Specify the size of each interrupt vector, which must be 4 or 16.
* **-mcache-block-size=**_num_  
  .IX Item "-mcache-block-size=num"
  Specify the size of each cache block,
  which must be a power of 2 between 4 and 512.
* **-march=**_arch_  
  .IX Item "-march=arch"
  Specify the name of the target architecture.
* **-mcmodel=**_code-model_  
  .IX Item "-mcmodel=code-model"
  Set the code model to one of
    * **small**  
      .IX Item "small"
      All the data and read-only data segments must be within 512KB addressing space.
      The text segment must be within 16MB addressing space.
    * **medium**  
      .IX Item "medium"
      The data segment must be within 512KB while the read-only data segment can be
      within 4GB addressing space.  The text segment should be still within 16MB
      addressing space.
    * **large**  
      .IX Item "large"
      All the text and data segments can be within 4GB addressing space.
* **-mctor-dtor**  
  .IX Item "-mctor-dtor"
  Enable constructor/destructor feature.
* **-mrelax**  
  .IX Item "-mrelax"
  Guide linker to relax instructions.

<a name="nios-s-1iis0-options"></a>

### Nios \s-1II\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "Nios II Options"
These are the options defined for the Altera Nios \s-1II\s0 processor.

* **-G** _num_  
  .IX Item "-G num"
  Put global and static objects less than or equal to _num_ bytes
  into the small data or \s-1BSS\s0 sections instead of the normal data or \s-1BSS\s0
  sections.  The default value of _num_ is 8.
* **-mgpopt=**_option_  
  .IX Item "-mgpopt=option"
* **-mgpopt**  
  .IX Item "-mgpopt"
* **-mno-gpopt**  
  .IX Item "-mno-gpopt"
  Generate (do not generate) GP-relative accesses.  The following 
  _option_ names are recognized:
    * **none**  
      .IX Item "none"
      Do not generate GP-relative accesses.
    * **local**  
      .IX Item "local"
      Generate GP-relative accesses for small data objects that are not 
      external, weak, or uninitialized common symbols.  
      Also use GP-relative addressing for objects that
      have been explicitly placed in a small data section via a \f(CW`section\*(C'
      attribute.
    * **global**  
      .IX Item "global"
      As for **local**, but also generate GP-relative accesses for
      small data objects that are external, weak, or common.  If you use this option,
      you must ensure that all parts of your program (including libraries) are
      compiled with the same **-G** setting.
    * **data**  
      .IX Item "data"
      Generate GP-relative accesses for all data objects in the program.  If you
      use this option, the entire data and \s-1BSS\s0 segments
      of your program must fit in 64K of memory and you must use an appropriate
      linker script to allocate them within the addressable range of the
      global pointer.
    * **all**  
      .IX Item "all"
      Generate GP-relative addresses for function pointers as well as data
      pointers.  If you use this option, the entire text, data, and \s-1BSS\s0 segments
      of your program must fit in 64K of memory and you must use an appropriate
      linker script to allocate them within the addressable range of the
      global pointer.
      .Sp
      **-mgpopt** is equivalent to **-mgpopt=local**, and
      **-mno-gpopt** is equivalent to **-mgpopt=none**.
      .Sp
      The default is **-mgpopt** except when **-fpic** or
      **-fPIC** is specified to generate position-independent code.
      Note that the Nios \s-1II ABI\s0 does not permit GP-relative accesses from
      shared libraries.
      .Sp
      You may need to specify **-mno-gpopt** explicitly when building
      programs that include large amounts of small data, including large
      \s-1GOT\s0 data sections.  In this case, the 16-bit offset for GP-relative
      addressing may not be large enough to allow access to the entire 
      small data section.
* **-mgprel-sec=**_regexp_  
  .IX Item "-mgprel-sec=regexp"
  This option specifies additional section names that can be accessed via
  GP-relative addressing.  It is most useful in conjunction with 
  \f(CW`section\*(C' attributes on variable declarations and a custom linker script.  
  The _regexp_ is a \s-1POSIX\s0 Extended Regular Expression.
  .Sp
  This option does not affect the behavior of the **-G** option, and 
  the specified sections are in addition to the standard \f(CW`.sdata\*(C'
  and \f(CW`.sbss\*(C' small-data sections that are recognized by **-mgpopt**.
* **-mr0rel-sec=**_regexp_  
  .IX Item "-mr0rel-sec=regexp"
  This option specifies names of sections that can be accessed via a 
  16-bit offset from \f(CW`r0\*(C'; that is, in the low 32K or high 32K 
  of the 32-bit address space.  It is most useful in conjunction with 
  \f(CW`section\*(C' attributes on variable declarations and a custom linker script.  
  The _regexp_ is a \s-1POSIX\s0 Extended Regular Expression.
  .Sp
  In contrast to the use of GP-relative addressing for small data, 
  zero-based addressing is never generated by default and there are no 
  conventional section names used in standard linker scripts for sections
  in the low or high areas of memory.
* **-mel**  
  .IX Item "-mel"
* **-meb**  
  .IX Item "-meb"
  Generate little-endian (default) or big-endian (experimental) code,
  respectively.
* **-march=**_arch_  
  .IX Item "-march=arch"
  This specifies the name of the target Nios \s-1II\s0 architecture.  \s-1GCC\s0 uses this
  name to determine what kind of instructions it can emit when generating
  assembly code.  Permissible names are: **r1**, **r2**.
  .Sp
  The preprocessor macro \f(CW`\_\|\_nios2\_arch\_\|\_\*(C' is available to programs,
  with value 1 or 2, indicating the targeted \s-1ISA\s0 level.
* **-mbypass-cache**  
  .IX Item "-mbypass-cache"
* **-mno-bypass-cache**  
  .IX Item "-mno-bypass-cache"
  Force all load and store instructions to always bypass cache by 
  using I/O variants of the instructions. The default is not to
  bypass the cache.
* **-mno-cache-volatile**  
  .IX Item "-mno-cache-volatile"
* **-mcache-volatile**  
  .IX Item "-mcache-volatile"
  Volatile memory access bypass the cache using the I/O variants of 
  the load and store instructions. The default is not to bypass the cache.
* **-mno-fast-sw-div**  
  .IX Item "-mno-fast-sw-div"
* **-mfast-sw-div**  
  .IX Item "-mfast-sw-div"
  Do not use table-based fast divide for small numbers. The default 
  is to use the fast divide at **-O3** and above.
* **-mno-hw-mul**  
  .IX Item "-mno-hw-mul"
* **-mhw-mul**  
  .IX Item "-mhw-mul"
* **-mno-hw-mulx**  
  .IX Item "-mno-hw-mulx"
* **-mhw-mulx**  
  .IX Item "-mhw-mulx"
* **-mno-hw-div**  
  .IX Item "-mno-hw-div"
* **-mhw-div**  
  .IX Item "-mhw-div"
  Enable or disable emitting \f(CW`mul\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`mulx\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`div\*(C' family of 
  instructions by the compiler. The default is to emit \f(CW`mul\*(C'
  and not emit \f(CW`div\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`mulx\*(C'.
* **-mbmx**  
  .IX Item "-mbmx"
* **-mno-bmx**  
  .IX Item "-mno-bmx"
* **-mcdx**  
  .IX Item "-mcdx"
* **-mno-cdx**  
  .IX Item "-mno-cdx"
  Enable or disable generation of Nios \s-1II R2 BMX\s0 (bit manipulation) and
  \s-1CDX\s0 (code density) instructions.  Enabling these instructions also
  requires **-march=r2**.  Since these instructions are optional
  extensions to the R2 architecture, the default is not to emit them.
* **-mcustom-**_insn_**=**_N_  
  .IX Item "-mcustom-insn=N"
* **-mno-custom-**_insn_  
  .IX Item "-mno-custom-insn"
  Each **-mcustom-**_insn_**=**_N_ option enables use of a
  custom instruction with encoding _N_ when generating code that uses 
  _insn_.  For example, **-mcustom-fadds=253** generates custom
  instruction 253 for single-precision floating-point add operations instead
  of the default behavior of using a library call.
  .Sp
  The following values of _insn_ are supported.  Except as otherwise
  noted, floating-point operations are expected to be implemented with
  normal \s-1IEEE 754\s0 semantics and correspond directly to the C operators or the
  equivalent \s-1GCC\s0 built-in functions.
  .Sp
  Single-precision floating point:
    * **fadds**, **fsubs**, **fdivs**, **fmuls**  
      .IX Item "fadds, fsubs, fdivs, fmuls"
      Binary arithmetic operations.
    * **fnegs**  
      .IX Item "fnegs"
      Unary negation.
    * **fabss**  
      .IX Item "fabss"
      Unary absolute value.
    * **fcmpeqs**, **fcmpges**, **fcmpgts**, **fcmples**, **fcmplts**, **fcmpnes**  
      .IX Item "fcmpeqs, fcmpges, fcmpgts, fcmples, fcmplts, fcmpnes"
      Comparison operations.
    * **fmins**, **fmaxs**  
      .IX Item "fmins, fmaxs"
      Floating-point minimum and maximum.  These instructions are only
      generated if **-ffinite-math-only** is specified.
    * **fsqrts**  
      .IX Item "fsqrts"
      Unary square root operation.
    * **fcoss**, **fsins**, **ftans**, **fatans**, **fexps**, **flogs**  
      .IX Item "fcoss, fsins, ftans, fatans, fexps, flogs"
      Floating-point trigonometric and exponential functions.  These instructions
      are only generated if **-funsafe-math-optimizations** is also specified.
      .Sp
      Double-precision floating point:
    * **faddd**, **fsubd**, **fdivd**, **fmuld**  
      .IX Item "faddd, fsubd, fdivd, fmuld"
      Binary arithmetic operations.
    * **fnegd**  
      .IX Item "fnegd"
      Unary negation.
    * **fabsd**  
      .IX Item "fabsd"
      Unary absolute value.
    * **fcmpeqd**, **fcmpged**, **fcmpgtd**, **fcmpled**, **fcmpltd**, **fcmpned**  
      .IX Item "fcmpeqd, fcmpged, fcmpgtd, fcmpled, fcmpltd, fcmpned"
      Comparison operations.
    * **fmind**, **fmaxd**  
      .IX Item "fmind, fmaxd"
      Double-precision minimum and maximum.  These instructions are only
      generated if **-ffinite-math-only** is specified.
    * **fsqrtd**  
      .IX Item "fsqrtd"
      Unary square root operation.
    * **fcosd**, **fsind**, **ftand**, **fatand**, **fexpd**, **flogd**  
      .IX Item "fcosd, fsind, ftand, fatand, fexpd, flogd"
      Double-precision trigonometric and exponential functions.  These instructions
      are only generated if **-funsafe-math-optimizations** is also specified.
      .Sp
      Conversions:
    * **fextsd**  
      .IX Item "fextsd"
      Conversion from single precision to double precision.
    * **ftruncds**  
      .IX Item "ftruncds"
      Conversion from double precision to single precision.
    * **fixsi**, **fixsu**, **fixdi**, **fixdu**  
      .IX Item "fixsi, fixsu, fixdi, fixdu"
      Conversion from floating point to signed or unsigned integer types, with
      truncation towards zero.
    * **round**  
      .IX Item "round"
      Conversion from single-precision floating point to signed integer,
      rounding to the nearest integer and ties away from zero.
      This corresponds to the \f(CW`\_\|\_builtin\_lroundf\*(C' function when
      **-fno-math-errno** is used.
    * **floatis**, **floatus**, **floatid**, **floatud**  
      .IX Item "floatis, floatus, floatid, floatud"
      Conversion from signed or unsigned integer types to floating-point types.
      .Sp
      In addition, all of the following transfer instructions for internal
      registers X and Y must be provided to use any of the double-precision
      floating-point instructions.  Custom instructions taking two
      double-precision source operands expect the first operand in the
      64-bit register X.  The other operand (or only operand of a unary
      operation) is given to the custom arithmetic instruction with the
      least significant half in source register _src1_ and the most
      significant half in _src2_.  A custom instruction that returns a
      double-precision result returns the most significant 32 bits in the
      destination register and the other half in 32-bit register Y.  
      \s-1GCC\s0 automatically generates the necessary code sequences to write
      register X and/or read register Y when double-precision floating-point
      instructions are used.
    * **fwrx**  
      .IX Item "fwrx"
      Write _src1_ into the least significant half of X and _src2_ into
      the most significant half of X.
    * **fwry**  
      .IX Item "fwry"
      Write _src1_ into Y.
    * **frdxhi**, **frdxlo**  
      .IX Item "frdxhi, frdxlo"
      Read the most or least (respectively) significant half of X and store it in
      _dest_.
    * **frdy**  
      .IX Item "frdy"
      Read the value of Y and store it into _dest_.
      .Sp
      Note that you can gain more local control over generation of Nios \s-1II\s0 custom
      instructions by using the \f(CW`target("custom-\f(CIinsn\f(CW=\f(CIN\f(CW")\*(C'
      and \f(CW`target("no-custom-\f(CIinsn\f(CW")\*(C' function attributes
      or pragmas.
* **-mcustom-fpu-cfg=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mcustom-fpu-cfg=name"
  This option enables a predefined, named set of custom instruction encodings
  (see **-mcustom-**_insn_ above).  
  Currently, the following sets are defined:
  .Sp
  **-mcustom-fpu-cfg=60-1** is equivalent to:
  -mcustom-fmuls=252 
  -mcustom-fadds=253 
  -mcustom-fsubs=254 
  -fsingle-precision-constant
  .Sp
  **-mcustom-fpu-cfg=60-2** is equivalent to:
  -mcustom-fmuls=252 
  -mcustom-fadds=253 
  -mcustom-fsubs=254 
  -mcustom-fdivs=255 
  -fsingle-precision-constant
  .Sp
  **-mcustom-fpu-cfg=72-3** is equivalent to:
  -mcustom-floatus=243 
  -mcustom-fixsi=244 
  -mcustom-floatis=245 
  -mcustom-fcmpgts=246 
  -mcustom-fcmples=249 
  -mcustom-fcmpeqs=250 
  -mcustom-fcmpnes=251 
  -mcustom-fmuls=252 
  -mcustom-fadds=253 
  -mcustom-fsubs=254 
  -mcustom-fdivs=255 
  -fsingle-precision-constant
  .Sp
  Custom instruction assignments given by individual
  **-mcustom-**_insn_**=** options override those given by
  **-mcustom-fpu-cfg=**, regardless of the
  order of the options on the command line.
  .Sp
  Note that you can gain more local control over selection of a \s-1FPU\s0
  configuration by using the \f(CW`target("custom-fpu-cfg=\f(CIname\f(CW")\*(C'
  function attribute
  or pragma.

These additional **-m** options are available for the Altera Nios \s-1II
ELF\s0 (bare-metal) target:

* **-mhal**  
  .IX Item "-mhal"
  Link with \s-1HAL BSP.\s0  This suppresses linking with the GCC-provided C runtime
  startup and termination code, and is typically used in conjunction with
  **-msys-crt0=** to specify the location of the alternate startup code
  provided by the \s-1HAL BSP.\s0
* **-msmallc**  
  .IX Item "-msmallc"
  Link with a limited version of the C library, **-lsmallc**, rather than
  Newlib.
* **-msys-crt0=**_startfile_  
  .IX Item "-msys-crt0=startfile"
  _startfile_ is the file name of the startfile (crt0) to use 
  when linking.  This option is only useful in conjunction with **-mhal**.
* **-msys-lib=**_systemlib_  
  .IX Item "-msys-lib=systemlib"
  _systemlib_ is the library name of the library that provides
  low-level system calls required by the C library,
  e.g. \f(CW`read\*(C' and \f(CW\*(C\`write\*(C'.
  This option is typically used to link with a library provided by a \s-1HAL BSP.\s0

<a name="nvidia-s-1ptxs0-options"></a>

### Nvidia \s-1PTX\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "Nvidia PTX Options"
These options are defined for Nvidia \s-1PTX:\s0

* **-m32**  
  .IX Item "-m32"
* **-m64**  
  .IX Item "-m64"
  Generate code for 32-bit or 64-bit \s-1ABI.\s0
* **-misa=**_ISA-string_  
  .IX Item "-misa=ISA-string"
  Generate code for given the specified \s-1PTX ISA\s0 (e.g. **sm\_35**).  \s-1ISA\s0
  strings must be lower-case.  Valid \s-1ISA\s0 strings include **sm\_30** and
  **sm\_35**.  The default \s-1ISA\s0 is sm_30.
* **-mmainkernel**  
  .IX Item "-mmainkernel"
  Link in code for a _\|_main kernel.  This is for stand-alone instead of
  offloading execution.
* **-moptimize**  
  .IX Item "-moptimize"
  Apply partitioned execution optimizations.  This is the default when any
  level of optimization is selected.
* **-msoft-stack**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-stack"
  Generate code that does not use \f(CW`.local\*(C' memory
  directly for stack storage. Instead, a per-warp stack pointer is
  maintained explicitly. This enables variable-length stack allocation (with
  variable-length arrays or \f(CW`alloca\*(C'), and when global memory is used for
  underlying storage, makes it possible to access automatic variables from other
  threads, or with atomic instructions. This code generation variant is used
  for OpenMP offloading, but the option is exposed on its own for the purpose
  of testing the compiler; to generate code suitable for linking into programs
  using OpenMP offloading, use option **-mgomp**.
* **-muniform-simt**  
  .IX Item "-muniform-simt"
  Switch to code generation variant that allows to execute all threads in each
  warp, while maintaining memory state and side effects as if only one thread
  in each warp was active outside of OpenMP \s-1SIMD\s0 regions.  All atomic operations
  and calls to runtime (malloc, free, vprintf) are conditionally executed (iff
  current lane index equals the master lane index), and the register being
  assigned is copied via a shuffle instruction from the master lane.  Outside of
  \s-1SIMD\s0 regions lane 0 is the master; inside, each thread sees itself as the
  master.  Shared memory array \f(CW`int \_\|\_nvptx\_uni[]\*(C' stores all-zeros or
  all-ones bitmasks for each warp, indicating current mode (0 outside of \s-1SIMD\s0
  regions).  Each thread can bitwise-and the bitmask at position \f(CW`tid.y\*(C'
  with current lane index to compute the master lane index.
* **-mgomp**  
  .IX Item "-mgomp"
  Generate code for use in OpenMP offloading: enables **-msoft-stack** and
  **-muniform-simt** options, and selects corresponding multilib variant.

<a name="openrisc-options"></a>

### OpenRISC Options

.IX Subsection "OpenRISC Options"
These options are defined for OpenRISC:

* **-mboard=**_name_  
  .IX Item "-mboard=name"
  Configure a board specific runtime.  This will be passed to the linker for
  newlib board library linking.  The default is \f(CW`or1ksim\*(C'.
* **-mnewlib**  
  .IX Item "-mnewlib"
  For compatibility, it's always newlib for elf now.
* **-mhard-div**  
  .IX Item "-mhard-div"
  Generate code for hardware which supports divide instructions.  This is the
  default.
* **-mhard-mul**  
  .IX Item "-mhard-mul"
  Generate code for hardware which supports multiply instructions.  This is the
  default.
* **-mcmov**  
  .IX Item "-mcmov"
  Generate code for hardware which supports the conditional move (\f(CW`l.cmov\*(C')
  instruction.
* **-mror**  
  .IX Item "-mror"
  Generate code for hardware which supports rotate right instructions.
* **-msext**  
  .IX Item "-msext"
  Generate code for hardware which supports sign-extension instructions.
* **-msfimm**  
  .IX Item "-msfimm"
  Generate code for hardware which supports set flag immediate (\f(CW`l.sf*i\*(C')
  instructions.
* **-mshftimm**  
  .IX Item "-mshftimm"
  Generate code for hardware which supports shift immediate related instructions
  (i.e. \f(CW`l.srai\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`l.srli\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`l.slli\*(C', \f(CW\*(C\`1.rori\*(C').  Note, to
  enable generation of the \f(CW`l.rori\*(C' instruction the **-mror** flag must
  also be specified.
* **-msoft-div**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-div"
  Generate code for hardware which requires divide instruction emulation.
* **-msoft-mul**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-mul"
  Generate code for hardware which requires multiply instruction emulation.

<a name="s-1pdp-11s0-options"></a>

### \s-1PDP\-11\s0 Options

.IX Subsection "PDP-11 Options"
These options are defined for the \s-1PDP-11:\s0

* **-mfpu**  
  .IX Item "-mfpu"
  Use hardware \s-1FPP\s0 floating point.  This is the default.  (\s-1FIS\s0 floating
  point on the \s-1PDP-11/40\s0 is not supported.)  Implies -m45.
* **-msoft-float**  
  .IX Item "-msoft-float"
  Do not use hardware floating point.
* **-mac0**  
  .IX Item "-mac0"
  Return floating-point results in ac0 (fr0 in Unix assembler syntax).
* **-mno-ac0**  
  .IX Item "-mno-ac0"
  Return floating-point results in memory.  This is the default.
* **-m40**  
  .IX Item "-m40"
  Generate code for a \s-1PDP-11/40.\s0  Implies -msoft-float -mno-split.
* **-m45**  
  .IX Item "-m45"
  Generate code for a \s-1PDP-11/45.\s0  This is the default.
* **-m10**  
  .IX Item "-m10"
  Generate code for a \s-1PDP-11/10.\s0  Implies -msoft-float -mno-split.
* **-mint16**  
  .IX Item "-mint16"
* **-mno-int32**  
  .IX Item "-mno-int32"
